title: Zero Knowledge Proofs and ZK Programming in Blockchain Application Development
description:
Zero knowledge proofs and SNARK systems are becoming one of the revolutionary technologies of the beginning of this century. In this workshop we will give a high-level introduction to the zero knowledge and SNARK technology stack from a software developer and IT professional perspectives with covering only slightly the deep mathematical basis. During the workshop we will implement an experimental zKRollup system in Circom on Hyperledger Besu.

**Agenda:**

1. A conceptual introduction to zero knowledge proofs (*45 min* \- presentation\)
A gentle introduction to prover, verifier, interactive versus non-interactive models, SNARKs, zkSNARKs, computation models, arithmetic circuits, rank-1 constraints, DLS languages and accumulators.

2. Introduction to Circom programming (*45 min* \- labs and Hands\-on\)
We will cover with lab exercises and hands-ons basic elements of the Circom programming language and the development flow including circuit and rank-1 constraint generation, compilation, power of tau, proving and verifying.
\- Break \+ discussion \(*15 min*)

3. zkRollups basics (*30 min* \- presentation\)
A general introduction to the conceptual elements of zero knowledge rollups.

4. Implementing a simplified zkRollup for token transfer and integrating with Hyperledger Besu or Fabric (*30 min* \- lab and demo\)
During the demonstration and lab we will implement a prototype zero knowledge rollup for a simplified token transfer and integrate it with Hyperledger Besu or Fabric.

5. Conclusions and discussion (*15 min +* )

**Workshop Leaders:**

* *[Andras Szabolcsi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andras-szabolcsi/):* Blockchain and solution expert, co-founder at BlockBen and Natrix. Highly skilled and experienced System and Solution Architect in the financial software developing industries.
* *[Daniel Szego](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daniel-szego/):* DLT Architect

title: Enfoque “Shift Left Ally”: moviendo la accesibilidad a la izquierda
description:
### **En Abstracta, creemos firmemente en la importancia de construir un mundo digital inclusivo y accesible para todas las personas.**

Por eso, te invitamos a un nuevo encuentro de Abstracta Tech Talks para profundizar sobre la temática, como parte de una serie de cuatro charlas que estaremos dando en mayo por el **Día Internacional de la Concientización de la Accesibilidad**.

**En esta instancia, Lisandra Armas Águila nos guiará en un viaje hacia la integración de la accesibilidad desde las primeras etapas del desarrollo de software.**

📅 **Fecha y Hora: 8 de mayo del 2024, 11 am.**
**Puedes inscribirte** \>\>[acá](https://forms.gle/z9g2RZAKgJPTegbG7)<<

Durante esta sesión, profundizaremos en:

* **La importancia de la accesibilidad**: buscaremos comprender por qué es crucial lograr que todos los sitios web y aplicaciones sean accesibles para todas personas, independientemente de sus condiciones, discapacidades o circunstancias.
* **El enfoque *Shift Left A11y***: exploraremos cómo integrar la accesibilidad como un elemento central desde el diseño hasta la implementación y las pruebas, ahorrando tiempo y recursos.
* **Cultura de accesibilidad en los equipos de desarrollo**: discutiremos cómo fomentar esta cultura involucrando a equipos de diseño, desarrollo y testing de accesibilidad desde el inicio.
* **Prácticas recomendadas y herramientas**: presentaremos herramientas y enfoques para facilitar la incorporación de la accesibilidad en las etapas iniciales del proceso de desarrollo.

Adoptar el enfoque *Shift Left A11y* no solo mejora la experiencia del usuario y promueve la inclusión digital, sino que también representa un paso adelante hacia un entorno de desarrollo más inclusivo.

**Te invitamos a ser parte de esta charla transformadora, que puede marcar un antes y un después en cómo abordar la accesibilidad en tus proyectos.**

### Sobre Lisandra

Graduada como Ingeniera de Software en 2011, Lisandra Armas Águila ha dedicado más de una década a la calidad del software. Específicamente, se especializó en accesibilidad y usabilidad. A través de cursos, artículos en su blog, y participaciones en charlas y talleres, Lisandra comparte su valioso conocimiento e impulsa un cambio positivo hacia la inclusión digital.

Por eso, como parte de nuestro ciclo de meetups de mayo por el Día Internacional de la Concientización de la Accesibilidad, te invitamos a un nuevo encuentro con la accesibilidad web como protagonista.

En esta instancia, el pionero en la automatización de la accesibilidad web **Leonardo Guedes** se enfocará en la importancia de automatizar las pruebas de accesibilidad. Ofrecerá una **demo sobre cómo la integración de axe-core con WebDriverIO puede transformar la manera en que realizamos pruebas en páginas web, para que sean accesibles para todas las personas.**

📅 **¿Cuándo? El 22 de mayo del 2024, a las 14 horas.**
**Para inscribirte puedes hacerlo >>[acá](https://forms.gle/KKNiKdQSkx8CztHB8)<<**

## Durante esta sesión, profundizaremos en:

* La **relevancia de automatizar** las pruebas de accesibilidad y cómo puede impactar positivamente en la experiencia de las personas que interactúan con los sistemas.
* Una **introducción a axe-core**: qué es y por qué es fundamental en el proceso de automatización de pruebas de accesibilidad.
* **Paso a paso** de la integración de axe-core con WebDriverIO para la automatización de pruebas.
* **Demostración en vivo** sobre la solución propuesta y los resultados obtenidos.

Al final de la presentación, tendrás la oportunidad de hacer preguntas y compartir tus opiniones, con el fin de que podamos enriquecer la experiencia de aprendizaje de manera conjunta.

**Te invitamos a ser parte de una nueva charla transformadora, que puede marcar un antes y un después en cómo abordar la accesibilidad en tus proyectos.**

## Sobre Leonardo

Con una trayectoria destacada como Test Automator, nuestro invitado ha dedicado gran parte de su carrera a las pruebas funcionales y automatizadas, tanto en aplicaciones web como móviles.

Su pasión por hacer la tecnología accesible a todas las personas lo ha llevado a profundizar en el campo de la accesibilidad web y a adquirir conocimientos sólidos a través de capacitaciones específicas y la aplicación práctica de herramientas como axe, Pa11y, WAVE y Google Lighthouse.

**¡Sigue a Leonardo en sus redes!** Te invitamos a seguir a nuestro ponente en [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/guedesrodriguezleonardo/) para seguir aprendiendo sobre estas temáticas.

¡No te pierdas esta oportunidad de enriquecer tu conocimiento y contribuir a un mundo digital más accesible!

title: Implementing IETF Secure Asset Transfer Protocol in Hyperledger Cacti Workshop
description:
In this workshop, participants will delve into the realm of blockchain and distributed ledger technology (DLT) interoperation by exploring the implementation of the IETF Secure Asset Transfer Protocol (SATP) within [Hyperledger Cacti](https://wiki.hyperledger.org/display/cactus/Hyperledger+Cacti+Home). The workshop will provide a comprehensive understanding of the concepts, architecture, and practical implementation aspects involved in standardizing the transfer of digital assets between diverse blockchain networks.

**Workshop Leaders:**

* [Venkatraman Ramakrishna](https://research.ibm.com/people/venkatraman-ramakrishna), Senior Researcher at IBM
* [Peter Somogyvari](https://www.linkedin.com/in/peter-somogyvari/), Software Product Architect at Accenture
* [Rafael Belchior](https://rafaelapb.github.io/), Ph.D. Student, Information Systems and Computer Engineering at INESC-ID & Técnico Lisboa, Portugal

**Key Topics Covered:**

1. Introduction to Hyperledger Cacti: Participants will gain insights into the functionality and architecture of Hyperledger Cacti, a platform facilitating digital asset transfers between different blockchain and DLT networks.
2. Overview of SATP: A detailed examination of the Secure Asset Transfer Protocol (SATP) developed under the auspices of the IETF. Participants will understand the significance of SATP in enabling seamless asset transfers between peer gateways across disparate networks.
3. Integration of SATP with Cacti: The workshop will focus on the implementation of the SATP draft specifications within the Hyperledger Cacti framework.
4. Demonstration of Asset Transfers: Practical demonstrations will showcase secure digital asset transfers using SATP within the Hyperledger Cacti environment. Participants will observe sample protocols in action and gain hands-on experience in executing cross-network asset transfers.

**Workshop Objectives:**

* Understand the challenges of blockchain/DLT interoperation and the role of standardized protocols in addressing them.
* Gain proficiency in using the SATP reference implementations within the Hyperledger Cacti ecosystem.
* Explore real-world use cases and scenarios for cross-network asset transfers facilitated by SATP.
* Contribute to the ongoing standardization efforts of SATP within the IETF framework through active participation and feedback.

**Target Audience:**
This workshop is designed for developers, blockchain enthusiasts, and enterprise stakeholders interested in enhancing their understanding of DLT interoperation and standardized asset transfer protocols. Prior knowledge of blockchain concepts and familiarity with Hyperledger Cacti will be beneficial but not mandatory.

**Pre-requisites:**

* Basic understanding of blockchain and distributed ledger technology.
* Familiarity with basic computer programming principles.
* Access to a development environment with
* Docker or other container engine installed
* At least 16 GB of RAM installed
* Proficiency in using command-line interfaces for executing setup and testing instructions.

Join us for an immersive journey into the world of blockchain interoperability and learn how Hyperledger Cacti, coupled with the SATP standard, is shaping the future of digital asset transfers across diverse networks.

title: La legislación en accesibilidad digital en Uruguay y su alcance
description:
En Abstracta Tech Talks, nos enorgullece ser un espacio donde la tecnología y la inclusión se encuentran. Por eso, este 29 de mayo del 2024, te invitamos a un encuentro especial que arrojará luz sobre un tema de vital importancia: la legislación en accesibilidad digital en Uruguay.

📅 **¿Cuándo? Miércoles 29 de mayo del 2024, a las 14 horas.**
**Puedes registrarte [\>\>Acá<<](https://forms.gle/YJhNxoc7wr742XHB9)**

Desde la aprobación de la ley sobre accesibilidad digital en Uruguay, se han dado pasos importantes. Sin embargo, aún queda un largo camino por recorrer. En este encuentro, Rossana Gienochio y Natalia Barrios, del Programa de Accesibilidad en Entornos Digitales de AGESIC, compartirán los pasos dados hasta ahora y abrirán un diálogo sobre los desafíos y oportunidades que se presentan hacia adelante.

**Durante esta sesión, exploraremos temas como:**
✅ Un repaso por la legislación actual en accesibilidad digital en Uruguay: ¿Qué dice la ley?
✅ Los avances logrados desde la aprobación de la ley: Un análisis de los pasos importantes dados hasta el momento.
✅ Los desafíos pendientes: ¿Qué obstáculos enfrentamos para una implementación efectiva de la accesibilidad digital?
✅ El futuro de la accesibilidad digital en Uruguay: Un diálogo sobre los próximos pasos y cómo podemos contribuir a ellos.

Este evento es una oportunidad única para comprender mejor cómo la legislación en accesibilidad digital está moldeando el futuro digital de Uruguay y cómo, de manera conjunta, podemos contribuir a un entorno digital más inclusivo.

**Biografías de las ponentes:**
Rossana Gienochio y Natalia Barrios son parte integral del equipo del Programa de Accesibilidad en Entornos Digitales en AGESIC. Con su dedicación y experiencia, han contribuido significativamente a la promoción y implementación de prácticas de accesibilidad digital en Uruguay, trabajando incansablemente para asegurar que los entornos digitales sean accesibles para todas las personas.

Te invitamos a seguir a nuestras ponentes y a unirte a nosotros en este diálogo esencial sobre la accesibilidad digital en Uruguay. Este 29 de mayo, sumérgete en una conversación que promete ser tan informativa como inspiradora. ¡Te esperamos!

title: Ver más allá de lo evidente. Los beneficios de Observabilidad en QA
description:
En Abstracta Tech Talks, siempre buscamos iluminar los rincones menos explorados de la tecnología y el desarrollo de software. Por eso, te invitamos a un encuentro que cambiará tu manera de ver y entender la Observabilidad dentro del mundo de QA. Con la guía de Leandro Melendez, un experto en el tema, descubrirás cómo esta práctica puede transformar no sólo tu trabajo, sino también aspectos cotidianos de tu vida.

📅 **Fecha:** 5 de junio del 2024
⏰ **Hora:** 18 hrs UYT
🖊️ **Registro:** Puedes registrarte [\>\>Acá<<](https://forms.gle/MThxq1nNXasRoB3f7)

Cuando usted escucha la palabra **"Observabilidad"** tal vez lo primero que le viene a la mente sea consumo de CPU, métricas de infraestructura, y temas relacionados con SRE.
Pero la observabilidad es mucho más que eso. Los beneficios y posibilidades son infinitos y muchas veces desconocidos.

La observabilidad puede ayudar a muchos problemas cotidianos del mundo de QA.

¿Sufre generando continuamente reportes para sus gerentes, o es usted el gerente que requiere estos informes? ¿Desconoce el estado de sus procesos de desarrollo o control de calidad? ¿Se desconocen o son difíciles de rastrear el estado de sus pipelines y los ciclos de DevOps? ¿Sabe dónde se atoran o abandonan los usuarios en su sistema? ¿Sabes si todavía queda leche en tu nevera?

A través de Observabilidad, puede resolver estos problemas en varias áreas de su negocio y de su vida. Esto es cierto especialmente en los procesos de control de calidad. La Observabilidad puede ir más allá y ayudar a sus equipos a estar al tanto de sus procesos de control de calidad sin iniciar sesión en sistemas propietarios, perder tiempo generando informes o conocimientos de plataformas especializadas.

**En esta charla aprenderás los principios, pilares y requisitos para implementar la Observabilidad** y aumentar tu conocimiento de la salud de tu sistema en cuanto a calidad se refiere.
**Obtendrá ejemplos de situaciones de la vida diaria, métricas de control de calidad, desarrollo, asuntos operativos y muchas otras áreas.**

Por último, **obtendrá consejos y trucos para implementar una excelente observabilidad en sus organizaciones, procesos de desarrollo, software y vida diaria.**

¡Después de esta charla verás las cosas de otra manera! ¡Desarrollarás la vista más allá de la vista!

**Sobre Leandro Melendez:**
Leandro Melendez, también conocido como Señor Performo, es un reconocido advocate en Grafana, dedicado a mejorar las prácticas de Observabilidad y rendimiento en la industria. Con una trayectoria de más de 10 años en pruebas de performance y 20 en el sector TI, Leandro ha colaborado con diversas empresas del S&P 500, aportando su vasta experiencia en tecnologías y lenguajes múltiples. Es el cerebro detrás del blog Señor Performo, anfitrión del podcast PerfBytes en español, y co-anfitrión de su versión en inglés. Además, Leandro comparte su conocimiento a través de presentaciones globales y contenido en video en su canal de YouTube. Es autor de "La Guía del Viajero de Proyectos de Carga" (The Hitchhicking Guide To Load Testing Projects), una guía divertida a través de las fases de un proyecto tradicional de pruebas de carga, disponible en [Amazon](https://amzn.to/37wqpyx).

**Conéctate con Leandro:**
\- YouTube: [[Señor Performo]](https://www.youtube.com/@SrPerfEsp?sub_confirmation=1)
\- LinkedIn: [[Leandro Melendez]](https://www.linkedin.com/in/leandromelendez/)
\- Twitter: [[@srperf]](https://twitter.com/srperf)

title: Hyperledger FireFly 1.3: What’s New and What’s Next
description:
Join us for an exciting webinar showcasing the latest release of [Hyperledger FireFly](https://github.com/hyperledger/firefly), version 1.3. Enhancements in this release make the industry’s first open source Web3 Gateway an even more powerful platform for developing interoperable, enterprise-grade digital asset and tokenization solutions.

In this webinar, Enrique Lacal, Hyperledger FireFly maintainer and Full Stack Engineer at Kaleido, will take you through all the latest features in the 1.3 release, including:

* **Namespace Isolation**: Ensuring high availability and seamless event replay
* **Invoke with Data**: Enable pinning off-chain data with a custom smart contract
* **Transaction Manager Enhancements**: Performance boosts, PostgreSQL support, and rich query APIs for improved diagnostics and usability
* **Hyperledger Besu Optimizations**: Making Besu and FireFly even better together with enhancements to performance and integration
* **Tezos Connector**: Enable seamless integration with Tezos chains, bringing all the benefits of Hyperledger FireFly to Tezos builders.

He’ll also demo the new functionality, and preview upcoming enhancements that the team is working on for future releases.

Don't miss this opportunity to explore Hyperledger FireFly v1.3. We look forward to seeing you there!

title: PAPER  READING GROUP #3
description:
Te invitamos a participar de la tercera sesión del club de lectua de papers.

Para la sesión del 20 de Junio vamos a revisar y discutir el paper **“Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series”** de los autores Abdul Fatir Ansari , Lorenzo Stella, Caner Turkmen, et al.

El parte es parte de los esfuerzos por desarrollar un modelo fundacional para series de tiempo, de la misma forma que se hizo en el mundo del lenguaje natural.

El paper sera guiado por Mauro Loprete.

Link: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.07815

\-\-\-\-\-\-

El Grupo de Lectura de Papers es una iniciativa de DataScience.uy dedicada al estudio e investigación académica en el campo del aprendizaje profundo y áreas relacionadas.

**Objetivo**

Fomentar discusiones interdisciplinarias y brindar a los participantes una sólida base de conocimientos en el área, al mismo tiempo democratizar el acceso al conocimiento y promover la comprensión de los conceptos fundamentales detrás de la Inteligencia Artificial y el Aprendizaje Automático.

La dinámica se desarrollará con la presentación de artículos, los cuales serán expuestos por miembros de la comunidad. Posteriormente, se lleva a cabo una discusión abierta entre todos los asistentes, donde se exploran y analizan en profundidad los aspectos relevantes de cada paper.

**Método y Formato**

* Presentación y discusión de papers fundamentales en el área de aprendizaje automático.
* Resumen, análisis de código y visualizaciones relacionadas con los artículos presentados.

**Cronograma**

El cronograma de cada sesión se organiza de la siguiente manera:

* 5 minutos: Introducción al tema, con el objetivo de facilitar la comprensión a aquellos participantes que no están familiarizados con el campo en cuestión.
* 25 minutos: Presentación del paper por parte del expositor.
* 60 minutos: Discusión abierta, donde todos los participantes pueden aportar comentarios, preguntas y reflexiones sobre el artículo presentado.

En cada sesión habrá un encargado de coordinar y facilitar las sesiones.

**Cómo participar**

Para participar en nuestras sesiones, te invitamos a seguir los siguientes pasos:

* Únete a este [link](https://join.slack.com/t/datascienceuy/shared_invite/zt-2jese13l0-OTVpxoz0XP672TmXMzvL5w) para interactuar y participar en él channel **#paper-reading-group** con el resto del grupo.
* Es requisito antes de cada sesión leer el paper que será discutido. Escribe tus ideas, reflexiones o preguntas y compartelas en la sesión.
* Sugiere papers para presentar en el canal de Slack para la siguiente sesión.

**Durante las sesiones**

Te alentamos a participar con comentarios y preguntas, con el fin de crear un ambiente fructífero y enriquecedor para todos. Ten en cuenta que el nivel de conocimiento de los participantes puede variar, por lo que el objetivo principal es disfrutar del proceso de aprendizaje y compartir conocimientos.

**Después de cada sesión**

Se buscá una persona voluntaria para exponer en la siguiente reunión. Además, valoramos tus comentarios y sugerencias, por lo que te invitamos a proporcionar feedback a través del siguiente formulario, así como a proponer nuevos papers para futuras discusiones.

Cualquier idea o sugerencia que tengas no dudes en compartirla en el slack con el resto de los miembros del grupo.

**¡Te esperamos!**

**• “Infinite Personalization with Diffusion Models”**
Speaker: Ramiro García
Description: In this talk, we’ll see an overview of diffusion models, explaining how they transform text into detailed images. You will learn how these models work, understand the underlying principles, and see practical demonstrations of controlling image generation with a single input. This session is perfect for those new to the topic and interested in using AI for personalized image creation. By the end, you will be equipped with the knowledge to start experimenting with diffusion models in your own projects.

**• “Back to Basics: NNX A new high level API for JAX and TPU v5"**
Speaker: David Cardozo
Description: In this talk we introduce NNX a Google DeepMind high level API that is at the backbone of many vision and multimodal models at Google and OpenSource, we will do an historical review with examples with the objective of launching a small tpuv5 training using Kubeflow and Vertex. This session is a good intro for practitioners and students interested in numerical and scientific computing and MLOps.

**👉 Sobre los oradores:**

**Ramiro García:** Currently based in Montevideo, Uruguay, Ramiro has extensive experience in tackling computer vision problems and has been working with diffusion models since their inception. Passionate about contributing to the community, he regularly shares his knowledge through videos and articles.

**David Cardozo:** Currently based in Quebec, Canada. David is passionate about multiplying matrices at universe scale. Advisor to many companies in the private and public sector, David is engaged with the open source community as a Google Developer Expert in AI, Docker Captain, and technical coach for machine learning engineers.

title: El Futuro del Trabajo y la GenIA.  Desafíos  riesgos y oportunidades.
description:
En Abstracta Tech Talks, nos apasiona explorar los temas más relevantes y disruptivos del mundo tecnológico. En esta ocasión, te invitamos a un panel imperdible donde discutiremos el impacto de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (GenAI) en el mundo del trabajo y cómo podemos prepararnos para este futuro.

**📅 ¿Cuándo? Miércoles 24 de julio de 2024, a las 14 h (UYT).**

### **¿Qué exploraremos juntos?**

* **Las habilidades humanas como complementarias:** Analizaremos cómo las habilidades humanas se complementan con la GenAI.
* **Delegación de tareas a la GenAI:** Discutiremos qué habilidades y tareas delegamos prontamente a la GenAI.
* **Impacto en el mundo del trabajo:** Exploraremos cómo la GenAI está transformando el entorno laboral y cómo podemos educarnos para adaptarnos a estos cambios.
* **Uso y confianza en GenAI:** Evaluaremos la forma de usar GenAI y cuánto confiamos en los resultados que genera.
* **Desafíos entre expectativas y realidad:** Abordaremos los desafíos que surgen entre las expectativas generadas por la GenAI y la realidad.
* **Riesgos de seguridad en GenAI:** Identificaremos los principales riesgos en la creación y uso de modelos de GenAI, con un enfoque en la seguridad.

### **Conoce más sobre nuestros panelistas:**

**Vera Babat**
Chief Culture Officer de Abstracta, psicóloga clínica y co-host de The Everything Else Podcast. Su misión es contribuir a desarrollar el potencial de cada integrante del equipo y, a nivel institucional, priorizar la dimensión humana de la empresa.
**[LinkedIn](https://uy.linkedin.com/in/vera-babat) \| [Twitter](https://twitter.com/VeraGoesTo)**

**Matías Reina**
Co-CEO y cofundador de Abstracta, Matías cuenta con 18 años de experiencia en tecnología de la información. Es graduado en Ingeniería en Computación de la Universidad de la República en Uruguay y es reconocido por su capacidad de innovación en productos relacionados con la calidad de software y soluciones basadas en GenAI.
**[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matiasreina/)**

**Sebastián Passarro**
Ingeniero en computación, Offensive Security Web Expert (OSWE), co-líder de OWASP Uruguay y líder de seguridad en GeneXus Consulting. Sebastián tiene una vasta experiencia en ciberseguridad y apoya a organizaciones como consultor en diversas tareas que abordan el ciclo de desarrollo seguro.
**[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sebastian-passaro/)**

### **¡No te lo pierdas!**

Te invitamos a seguir a nuestros panelistas en sus redes sociales para estar al tanto de sus últimas novedades y contribuciones en el campo de la tecnología y la GenAI. **¡Nos vemos en el evento!**

title: Elixir Montevideo Meetup - Agosto 2024
description:
¡Te invitamos a la reunión de desarrolladores de **Elixir de Montevideo**!
Vuelven las meetups de Elixir luego de casi 2 años sin actividad!
El formato va a ser de 2 charlas de \~30min cada una, con un break en el medio

Agenda:
-> **Elixir y TDD: Los mejores amigos de un desarrollador por Andres Ruiz**
Sumérgete al mundo del Desarrollo Guiado por Pruebas (TDD) en Elixir, donde la filosofía se encuentra con la practicidad y el código es tan robusto como elegante. En esta charla, exploraremos la esencia de las pruebas unitarias y la delgada línea entre muchas y pocas pruebas.
Usando casos reales, exploraremos el arte de crear pruebas que minimicen el estrés y maximicen el descanso. (Porque seamos sinceros, a nadie le gusta depurar código a las 2 de la mañana).

Prepárate para desafiar la sabiduría convencional mientras abordamos una pregunta crítica: ¿Cuántas pruebas son suficientes? Aprende cómo hablar con la gerencia demostrando los beneficios innegables de una base de código bien probada. Discutiremos los peligros ocultos de descuidar las pruebas y cómo el TDD en un lenguaje funcional como Elixir transforma la experiencia de testing en un proceso fluido y agradable.

Ya seas un veterano del TDD o un novato curioso, esta sesión te entretendrá, provocará debates y, con suerte, te dará ideas para mejorar tus habilidades de testing. Descubre cómo dominar el TDD en Elixir puede hacerte un mejor desarrollador y, quién sabe, quizás hasta una mejor persona.

-> **Meetup Bot: De Ruby a Elixir por marpo60**

Si tenés una charla, algo que aprendiste o que estás probando con Elixir, te invitamos a que lo compartas, escribinos.
Los esperamos!

title: IA responsable: Ética y desafíos en un mundo de algoritmos desobedientes
description:
Te invitamos a una charla seguida de una sesión de intercambio, donde exploraremos cómo abordar los aspectos éticos y los desafíos específicos de la inteligencia artificial (IA) desde la perspectiva de los testers de software. Hablaremos sobre la **importancia de la ética en el desarrollo y prueba de sistemas de IA, incluyendo estrategias para gestionar el sesgo algorítmico, proteger la privacidad y asegurar la transparencia y la responsabilidad en los modelos de IA**. También discutiremos los **desafíos técnicos y sociales** que enfrentamos en el desarrollo y testing de soluciones que usan IA.

Esta charla está diseñada para generar una discusión profunda y significativa sobre cómo enfrentar estos retos. La sesión de intercambio será una oportunidad para debatir, compartir experiencias y resolver dudas con otros profesionales del testing y el desarrollo.

📅 **¿Cuándo?** Miércoles 7 de agosto de 2024, a las 14 h (UY).

**Temas a tratar:**
- **Ética en el desarrollo y prueba de sistemas de IA:** Importancia y estrategias.
- **Gestión del sesgo algorítmico:** Cómo identificar y mitigar sesgos en los modelos de IA.
- **Protección de la privacidad:** Técnicas para asegurar la privacidad en sistemas de IA.
- **Transparencia y responsabilidad:** Cómo garantizar que los modelos de IA sean transparentes y responsables.
- **Desafíos técnicos y sociales:** Problemas y soluciones en el desarrollo y testing de IA.

**Para conocer un poco sobre Lorena:**
Lorena Etcheverry Venturini es Ingeniera en Computación por la Facultad de Ingeniería (UdelaR) y Doctora en Informática por el PEDECIBA-UdelaR. Actualmente, es Profesora Agregada (Gr4) en el Instituto de Computación de la Facultad de Ingeniería (FING). Es investigadora Nivel I del Sistema Nacional de Investigadores (SNI) e investigadora Grado 3 del PEDECIBA Informática. Además, coordina la Maestría en Ciencias de Datos y Aprendizaje Automático de la FING e integra el Centro Interdisciplinario en Ciencia de Datos de la UdelaR (CICADA.uy).
Lorena ha participado desde su creación en 2011 en el Grupo de Trabajo sobre Datos Abiertos coordinado por AGESIC. Su área de interés es la gestión de datos, especialmente la calidad de datos, las bases de datos de grafos, los grafos de conocimiento y los sistemas de análisis de datos. Más recientemente, se ha dedicado a aspectos éticos y de privacidad en la ciencia de datos, específicamente a la anonimización de datos y a técnicas analíticas que preservan la privacidad, así como a la detección y mitigación de sesgos algorítmicos. Lorena dirige y participa en proyectos de investigación en estas temáticas, y es coautora de varios artículos publicados en revistas científicas y anales de conferencias internacionales.

title: Potenciales usos de GenAI en empresas TI sin saber programar
description:
Como parte de nuestra serie de charlas en Abstracta, dedicaremos un episodio a **un tema que ha revolucionado nuestra forma de trabajar en Abstracta: el uso de Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (GenAI)** sin la necesidad de saber programar, con la participación de **Natalie Rodgers.**

¿En qué áreas estamos utilizando la GenAI? ¿Cuáles son los beneficios? ¿Cómo estamos haciendo para potenciar nuestros resultados? **Nos adentraremos en aplicaciones claves que estamos implementando en Abstracta**, para comprender cómo impacta en la eficiencia y calidad de trabajo de diferentes áreas de la empresa.

**La presentación incluirá los siguientes temas:**

✅**Reportes técnicos:** cómo universalizamos la experiencia, unificamos nuestra voz y mejoramos la comunicación corporativa.
✅**Optimización de contenidos:** cómo agilizamos la creación de contenidos técnicos y case studies, con una voz escalable, y prácticas de UX Writing y SEO.
✅**People Care:** cómo utilizamos la IA generativa para la Wiki, mapa de ruta y Compass, con foco en nuestra cultura humanista.
✅**Demos en vivo:** ejemplos prácticos con casos de uso destacados.

📅 **¿Cuándo? Miércoles 21 de agosto, a las 14 h horas (UY)**

¿Te sumás?

**Biografía de la ponente:**
Con más de 15 años de experiencia en la creación de contenidos, **Natalie Rodgers es periodista y Licenciada en Comunicación Audiovisual.** Ha trabajado en múltiples áreas dentro de su campo de estudio: investigación periodística, redacción tanto técnica como creativa, comunicación corporativa, UX Writing, Social Media, ghostwriting y más.

Se considera una apasionada por su profesión, con gran interés por la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (GenAI) y por ser parte de proyectos que buscan impactar de manera positiva en nuestra sociedad.

Desde 2021, trabaja como **Content Manager y Generative AI Content Specialist en la empresa de creación de software Abstracta**, con sedes en Chile, Colombia, Estados Unidos y Uruguay.

Actualmente, lidera un área de Abstracta desde la cual ofrecen **servicios de UX Content Design.** Apoyan a las empresas en la creación de estrategias y desarrollo de las mismas para generar contenidos impactantes y escalables con apoyo de la GenAI, que ayuden a cumplir sus objetivos de manera sostenible, eficiente, efectiva y disfrutable.

description:
Este es un evento organizado por la comunidad de Meetups de desarrollo del Uruguay. Más info, registro y reserva de la entrada en la página del evento: https://www.owu.uy/la-meetup

**La Meetup** ofrece un espacio para reunirnos en persona y conectar con comunidades de tecnología locales.
Este evento será un punto de encuentro para profesionales, estudiantes y entusiastas de la tecnología de todo el país. Es una grán oportunidad para intercambiar ideas, compartir experiencias y construir relaciones que fomenten el crecimiento y la unidad dentro de la comunidad tecnológica uruguaya.

**¿En qué consiste?**
Es una conferencia o reunión abierta, donde la principal característica es que la agenda se genera de manera dinámica entre todos los participantes de la reunión.

**Etapas:**

* **↪ Apertura**: El facilitador explica la estructura y mecánica del espacio.
* **↪ Mercado de Ideas**: Los participantes pueden proponer tópicos de interés y se organizan en un tablero de anuncios.
* **↪ Sesiones de Discusión**: Se llevan a cabo conversaciones del tópico seleccionado, los participantes se auto-organizan en los lugares predefinidos.
* **↪ Clausura**: Al finalizar todas las sesiones y con ayuda del facilitador, los participantes se reúnen nuevamente para realizar el cierre del espacio.

title: Elixir Montevideo Meetup - Octubre 2024
description:
¡Te invitamos a la reunión de desarrolladores de **Elixir de Montevideo**!
Vuelven las meetups de Elixir luego de casi 2 años sin actividad!
El formato va a ser de 2 charlas de \~30min cada una, con un break en el medio

Agenda:
-> **Restauración de imágenes defectuosas con Elixir Nx por Santiago Imelio**
Elixir Nx es un proyecto activamente desarrollado que tiene como objetivo incorporar capacidades de cálculo numérico y álgebra lineal en Elixir. Este ecosistema ha dado lugar a varias librerías que, en conjunto, proporcionan poderosas herramientas para el desarrollo en áreas como ciencia de datos y machine learning.En esta charla vamos a explorar algunos conceptos básicos de la principal librería numérica de Elixir, Nx, a través de una aplicación práctica en el área de procesamiento de imágenes. Implementaremos una variante del filtro de mediana, tomando provecho de las características de Nx para lograr un rendimiento eficiente.

-> **Elixir, Language Servers, Phoenix y la marencoche por Nicolas Ferraro**
Te parece mala la developer experience cuando usas Phoenix? Cansado/a de no tener autocomplete en tus templates? Nunca te acordás de los paths de tus rutas cuando tiras un `~p` ? Ayudame a mejorarla mediante con la implementación de un language server.La idea de esta charla es introducir el concepto de LSP y language servers, ver cómo funcionan los que existen hoy en día para Elixir, definir como podríamos implementar uno para hacernos la vida más fácil y ver cómo podemos abordar esto como un proyecto hobby.

Si nos da el tiempo mostrar algunos ejemplos de código y cerrar con una demostración de como funcionaría el servidor cuando se integra con un editor de texto.

Si tenés una charla, algo que aprendiste o que estás probando con Elixir, te invitamos a que lo compartas, escribinos.
Los esperamos!

title: Besu Plug-ins Workshop: Fork-free Client Modifications to Extend Besu Use Cases
description:
Besu is an Ethereum client designed to be enterprise-friendly for both public and private permissioned network use cases, with an extractable EVM implementation.

Join us for an in-depth exploration of Besu plug-ins, where we’ll unveil how the plug-ins can enable fork-free client modifications to extend Besu’s use cases. We will dive into real-world examples, showcase the flexibility of the plug-in framework, and discuss best practices for maintaining seamless compatibility while extending Besu to meet specific network requirements. Don’t miss this opportunity to discover how to maximize Besu’s potential through innovative, non-disruptive client modifications.

This workshop is tailored for developers, architects, and blockchain enthusiasts who want to enhance their understanding of Besu’s architecture and learn how to implement custom features without the need for forking the client, modifying source code, or developing bespoke solutions.

Speakers:
[Justin Florentine](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinflorentine/), Staff Protocol Engineer for Besu at ConsenSys
[Daniel Lehrner](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daniel-lehrner-994170293/), Staff Blockchain Protocol Engineer

title: Webinar with TOIP-Verifiable Authenticity to Address the Threat of AI Deep Fakes
description:
Join us for an in-depth webinar Trust over IP (ToIP) to explore how cryptographic proof can preserve authenticity online in the age of generative AI. As generative AI accelerates, it will become all but impossible to detect who and what is authentic online. The only solution is cryptographic proof: digital credentials that prove you are a real person, a real company, or that you have authored real content (sites, documents, photos, videos, etc.) The smartest AI in the world cannot fake such proofs. Trust Over IP (ToIP) has been laying the foundation to put that capability in the hands of every person, organization, and government using the Internet. This webinar will share the latest developments in the ToIP model for decentralized digital trust infrastructure, including the Trust Spanning Protocol (TSP), the Trust Registry Query Protocol (TRQP), and governance models for digital trust ecosystems. We will also dive into what this means for specific ecosystems such as financial services, CBDCs, workforces, and even nation states like Bhutan and Switzerland.

The webinar will take place on November 13 at 10AM PT/1 PM ET/7PM CET

title: AI Alliance: Getting Started with Docling and Data Prep Kit
description:
**Data Prep Kit** is a robust, open-source Python toolkit designed to simplify and accelerate data preparation for diverse use cases. It provides out-of-the-box support for common data preparation tasks and is designed to scale seamlessly from a personal laptop to large cloud-based clusters. Key features include document deduplication, handling both documents and code, language detection (spoken and programming languages), PII removal, spam and hate speech detection, and malware detection in code.

One of the key components of the Data Prep Kit is **Docling**, a versatile document processor capable of handling multiple formats such as PDF, HTML, and DOCX. By integrating with Docling, Data Prep Kit ensures seamless parsing of supported file types, making it an indispensable tool for data scientists and ML engineers.

In this talk, I will introduce the capabilities of Data Prep Kit and Docling, walk you through their key features, and demonstrate how to get started with these powerful tools to streamline your data preparation workflows.

* Learn more about Data Prep Kit: https://github.com/IBM/data-prep-kit
* Learn more about Docling: https://github.com/DS4SD/docling

**Session Type**
Talk / Hands on Workshop (hybrid)

**Audience**
LLM app developers, data scientists, data engineers

**Technical Level**
Beginner - Intermediate

**Prerequisites**
A Python development environment is strongly recommended for this workshop. Step-by-step instructions for setting up the environment will be provided.

**Industry**
Cross industry

**Agenda**

* Welcome & introductions (5')
* About the AI Alliance & how you can get involved (5')
* Main talk: “Getting Started with Docling and Data Prep Kit” (30')
* Q&A
* Closing

**About the instructor**
[Sujee Maniyam](https://sujee.dev/bio-sujee.html) (AI Engineer, Developer Advocate @ Node51) is an expert in Generative AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Big Data, Distributed Systems, and Cloud technologies. He is passionate about developer education, fostering community engagement. Sujee has led numerous training sessions, hackathons, and workshops. He is also an author, open source contributor and frequent speaker at conferences and meetups.

**About the AI Alliance**
The [AI Alliance](https://thealliance.ai) is an international community of researchers, developers and organizational leaders committed to support and enhance open innovation across the AI technology landscape to accelerate progress, improve safety, security and trust in AI, and maximize benefits to people and society everywhere. Members of the AI Alliance believe that open innovation is essential to develop and achieve safe and responsible AI that benefit society rather than benefit a select few big players.

title: [AI Alliance] RAG pipeline With Data Prep Kit + Milvus + Granite (Workshop)
description:

Noteworthy features of DPK include:

* de-duping documents (exact dedupe and fuzzy dedupe),

* language detection (spoken languages and programming languages),

title: De Testing Tradicional a Automatización y Pruebas en IA: Retos y Oportunidesade
description:
Como parte de nuestra serie de Abstracta Tech Talks, te invitamos a un evento imperdible donde exploraremos la evolución del testing tradicional hacia la automatización y las pruebas en inteligencia artificial. Contaremos con la participación de **Rocío Del Pilar Correa Malagon,** una experta en el campo, quien compartirá su experiencia y conocimientos.

**📅 ¿Cuándo? Miércoles 5 de marzo de 2025, a las 13:00 horas (UY). Para registrarte puedes hacerlo [acá](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfndCW7PCVlsxarL2_REP88kAQu9P6dry-LYdYjy5dLp-rm0g/viewform?usp=sharing).**

### **Temas a tratar:**

* **Evolución del Testing Tradicional a la Automatización:** Exploraremos los desafíos y consideraciones clave en este proceso.
* **Primeros Pasos en la Automatización:** Discutiremos cómo iniciar en la automatización y qué factores tener en cuenta.
* **Pruebas de Software en Aplicaciones con IA:** Analizaremos cómo las pruebas de software han evolucionado para adaptarse a aplicaciones que utilizan modelos de inteligencia artificial.
* **Relación entre Automatización de Pruebas y IA:** Destacaremos el impacto en la calidad del software y cómo los equipos de testing pueden prepararse para el futuro.
* **Estrategias de Capacitación en IA:** Hablaremos sobre las habilidades necesarias para enfrentar los nuevos retos en la industria.
* **Guía Práctica para la Automatización y Validación de Modelos de IA:** Proporcionaremos las mejores prácticas y oportunidades en este campo en constante evolución.

### **Biografía de la ponente:**

Rocío Del Pilar Correa Malagon es especialista en testing de software con 17 años de experiencia en industrias como banca, retail, e-commerce, salud y automotriz. Ha trabajado en aplicaciones web, móviles y ciberseguridad, enfocándose en la implementación de buenas prácticas en testing tradicional. Su experiencia abarca pruebas manuales, análisis de requerimientos y aseguramiento de calidad.
En los últimos años, Rocío ha expandido su expertise hacia la automatización de pruebas, explorando herramientas y metodologías para optimizar procesos y mejorar la eficiencia en la validación del software. Su profundo conocimiento en el sector bancario le ha permitido adquirir una sólida base en el aseguramiento de calidad de software crítico.

title: Integrating Fabric Private Chaincode with Hyperledger CC-Tools
description:
Hyperledger Fabric is a widely adopted enterprise blockchain framework, but privacy concerns remain a challenge in many use cases. [Fabric Private Chaincode](https://github.com/hyperledger/fabric-private-chaincode) (FPC) extends Fabric’s capabilities by enabling **confidential smart contract execution** using trusted execution environments (TEEs). Meanwhile, [CC Tools](https://github.com/hyperledger-labs/cc-tools) simplifies the development, deployment, and testing of Fabric chaincode, including FPC.

In this session, we will explore:

* What Fabric Private Chaincode (FPC) is and how it ensures confidential transactions
* The role of CC Tools in managing chaincode development and deployment
* How to integrate FPC and CC Tools effectively in a Hyperledger Fabric network
* A live demonstration showcasing private smart contract execution

This talk is ideal for blockchain developers, architects, and DevOps engineers interested in **enhancing privacy in enterprise blockchain applications**. Join us to gain hands-on insights into securing smart contracts on Hyperledger Fabric!

title: [AI Alliance] Workshop: Hands-on with Data Prep Kit
description:
**Overview**
When building machine learning and data applications, a significant portion of your time will be dedicated to data wrangling - from content extraction and cleaning to de-duplication and filtering out problematic data. In this hands-on session we will explore Data Prep Kit - an open source toolkit, designed to streamline these essential tasks. Attendees will learn first hand how to use the Data Prep Kit to accelerate data preparation, improve overall data quality, and enhance the efficiency of building robust LLM applications.

**Description**
Data Prep Kit is a comprehensive Python library that democratizes and accelerates data preparation by providing out-of-the-box solutions for common tasks. Engineered to scale from a single laptop to large cloud clusters, it has been successfully used to process terabytes of data for training IBM Granite Large Language Models (LLMs).

Data Prep Kit offers a robust feature set including duplicate elimination, advanced document and code handling, language detection (for both spoken and programming languages), removal of personally identifiable information (PII), as well as spam, hate speech, and malware detection.

More about Data Prep Kit : https://github.com/IBM/data-prep-kit

Join us for this hands-on session to explore how to use Data Prep Kit to accelerate data preparation, enhance data quality.

In this workshop we will do the following:

* getting started with Data Prep Kit
* Extract content from various documents (PDFs, DOCX, HTML)
* Cleanup documents by removing excess markup
* Detect and remove duplicate documents
* Detect and remove low quality and spam documents

title: [AI Alliance] Hyper Parameter Optimization for Computer Vision using TerraTorch
description:
**Hyper Parameter Optimization, Neural Architecture Search and Foundation Model Benchmarking using TerraTorch for (geospatial) computer vision**
[TerraTorch](https://thealliance.ai/affiliated-projects/terratorch) is a fine-tuning and benchmarking toolkit for Geospatial Foundation Models built on PyTorch Lightning and tailored for satellite, weather, and climate data. It integrates domain-specific data modules, pre-defined tasks, and a modular model factory that pairs any backbone with diverse decoder heads. These components allow researchers and practitioners to fine-tune supported models in a no-code fashion by simply editing a training or inference configuration. By consolidating best practices for model development and incorporating the automated hyperparameter optimization extension Iterate, TerraTorch reduces the expertise and time required to fine-tune or benchmark models on new Earth Observation use cases. Furthermore, TerraTorch directly integrates with GEO-Bench, allowing for systematic and reproducible benchmarking of Geospatial Foundation Models. TerraTorch Iterate is not only driving GeoBench, but also Hyperparameter Optimizations (HPO) and Neural Architecture Search (NAS). TerraTorch is open sourced under Apache 2.0, and can be installed via pip install terratorch from our Github repostitory.

**Highlights**

* Growing list of IBM and community Out-of-the-box implementations of foundation models (e.g.Prithvi, Satlas, Clay, timm models) and a large selection of decoders
* Model fine-tuning fully accessible through config files – no need to write code for segmentation, pixel-wise regression, object detection or classification tasks
* The functionalities of TerraTorch are a superset of Lightning and TorchGeo. All the goodies from these libraries come for free

**Agenda**

1. Welcome & introductions
2. Short recap on cuda, torch and lightning
3. What are (geospatial) computer vision foundation models
4. Finetuning and Inference
5. Hyperparameter Optimization with terratorch iterate using optuna
6. Benchmarking foundation models
7. Q&A
8. Closing

Romeo is an AI Research Engineer at IBM Research Europe in Zurich interested in understanding neural representations in artificial and biological neural networks.

title: [AI Alliance] AI Red-Teaming: Stress Testing AI Systems for Safety & Reliability
description:
In this talk, we’ll explore the critical role of AI red-teaming in ensuring the safety, security, and reliability of AI systems. As AI adoption accelerates, adversarial testing has become essential to uncover vulnerabilities, mitigate risks, and build trustworthy models. We'll discuss practical red-teaming strategies for identifying model weaknesses, from prompt injection attacks to harmful content generation. Drawing on insights from HydroX AI’s automated red-teaming platform and our work with partners like Anthropic, I'll highlight best practices for developers, AI engineers, and business leaders to integrate red-teaming into their development lifecycle. The session will provide actionable guidance for both open-source projects and enterprise AI deployments.

title: [AI Alliance] Chat with your website using an LLM
description:
**Abstract**
Imagine being able to ask questions about a website in natural language—and receiving meaningful answers instead of simple keyword matches. In this talk, I’ll introduce Allycat, an open-source, end-to-end stack that enables conversational interaction with website content using Large Language Models (LLMs).

We’ll walk through the complete pipeline:

* Crawling and indexing website content
* Cleaning and extracting meaningful information from HTML
* Creating embeddings and storing them in a vector database
* Querying the data using an LLM for contextual, accurate responses

We’ll also demonstrate Allycat’s lightweight UI that allows users to interactively test their queries. The entire stack is built with Python and open-source components, making it easy to adopt, adapt, and extend.

You can checkout Allycat here : [https://github.com/The-AI-Alliance/allycat](https://github.com/The-AI-Alliance/allycat)

**Audience**
AI/ML Engineers, Data Engineers, Data Scientists interested in building intelligent, LLM-powered search and chatbot interfaces.

**Level**
Beginner to Intermediate

**Format**
45-minute presentation with demonstration

**About the speaker**

**MatExpert: Decomposing Materials Discovery by Mimicking Human Experts**
For accelerated inorganic materials design, a framework capable of AI-driven exploration of the vast materials spaces across the periodic table is required. In this talk, I will introduce MatAgent, a generative AI agent for inorganic materials design mimicking the reasoning process of human experts. description:

**Unlocking Guidance for Discrete State-Space Diffusion and Flow Models**
Many scientific tasks, such as protein engineering and small-molecule drug discovery, can be formulated as conditional generation problems over discrete spaces. This talk introduces a new approach that enables tractable classifier and classifier-free guidance on discrete state-space diffusion and flow models. I will demonstrate how this method can be applied for conditional generation tasks in protein sequence, small-molecule graph, and DNA sequence design.

title: [AI Alliance] Model and Agent Evaluation with Unitxt
description:
**Description**
Evaluating the performance of language models and AI agents can be challenging, especially across diverse tasks and domains. In this session, we'll introduce [Unitxt](https://www.unitxt.ai), an open-source framework for unified text evaluation, and explore how it simplifies the process of benchmarking LLMs and agents using a standardized format.

We'll walk through the core ideas behind LLM evaluation—what to measure, how to measure it, and why it matters—and then dive into hands-on examples of evaluating LLMs for quality, reliability, safety and more, as well as evaluating multi-modalities and agentic tool invocation.
Whether you're just getting started with evaluation or looking for a powerful and flexible tool to streamline your workflows, this session will offer practical insights and code-based demos to help you get up and running.

Bring your questions, ideas, or examples—we’ll have time for discussion and Q&A at the end!

**Speaker Bio**
Elron Bandel ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/elron/)) works to redefine how language models are tested and used at scale. At IBM Research, he leads projects that enhance researchers' abilities to test and utilize language models at transformative scales. Elron co-authored IBM's standard evaluation platform for large language models and spearheads the development of Unitxt, an open-source Python library for AI performance assessment. His academic record supervised by Prof. Yoav Goldberg included work on developing AlephBERT and its innovative evaluation suite, and research into robust language model testing.

title: [AI Alliance] Knowledge Graphs for Enterprise AI
description:
**Description**
[Proscenium](https://the-ai-alliance.github.io/proscenium/) is an emerging library of composable glue focused on enterprise AI applications. It prioritizes support for domains where the creation and use of structured data is critical. This talk will walk through the construction an application for the legal domain built with Proscenium that involves:

1. Document enrichment
2. Entity resolution
3. Knowledge Graph construction
4. Query handling
5. Chat integration

Finally, we'll cover the future roadmap and ways that you could contribute!

**Speaker Bio**
Adam Pingel ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adampingel/), [GitHub](https://github.com/adampingel)) is IBM's Head of Open Tools and Applications for the [AI Alliance](https://thealliance.ai). Adam has been fascinated by AI and chatbots since playing with [Racter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racter) in the 80’s. But the “winters” were long and frequent. The stars aligned in 2015 when he became VPE at Ravel Law. Ravel was building AI-powered tools for the legal industry and was working with Harvard Law School on what is now known as the Caselaw Access Project. After an acquisition by LexisNexis in 2017, he moved his family to Raleigh (in 2019) to take the role of CTO of Global Platforms. In 2022 he joined IBM to work on domain-specific applications of generative AI. Adam holds an MS and BS in CS from UCLA and Stanford, respectively. When not at a keyboard, he enjoys spending time with his family.

title: How Socious Builds Digital Identity Solutions Using Hyperledger Identus
description:
[Socious](https://socious.io/) will be taking center stage at the upcoming Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust meetup, showcasing their groundbreaking approach to digital identity and how they are leveraging the [Hyperledger Identus project](https://github.com/hyperledger-identus).

Their innovative solution tackles two real-world challenges that plague both organizations and individuals: the tedious, time-consuming nature of background verification and the privacy concerns surrounding age verification. By transforming university diplomas and professional certifications into secure verifiable credentials, Socious eliminates redundant background checks while preserving trust.

Perhaps most compelling is their elegant implementation of selective disclosure for age verification—allowing users to prove they meet age requirements without surrendering complete ID scans or excessive personal information. As digital identity moves from theoretical discussions to practical applications, Socious demonstrates how decentralized technology can simultaneously enhance efficiency, maintain trust, and protect privacy in ways previously thought impossible.

title: [AI Alliance] Introducing RAGme-ai
description:
[RAGme-ai](https://github.com/maximilien/ragme-ai) is a personalized RAG agent for the web sites you visit and care about.

Use cases include:

1. Interractive personal RAG adding web sites and documents and using an LLM agent to query
2. Collecting web sites or documents on a particular topic and RAGing and searching them
3. Collecting posts from a blog and RAGing and searching them
4. Collecting visited sites from a user's daily activities and RAGing and searching them
5. Collecting documents from a user and RAGing and searching them

RAGing and searching refers to adding documents into a Vector database using some appropriate embedding (process to RAG) and then using an LLM agent to query and use that database as source of knowledge.

Max. Hacker.
IBM Research.

* Financial Operations (#FinOps)
* Compliance & Security Operations (#CISO)

* Join the AI Alliance Discord: https://discord.gg/ntG3yqSr

**About the AI Alliance**

The [AI Alliance](https://thealliance.ai) is an international community of researchers, developers and organizational leaders committed to support and enhance open innovation across the AI technology landscape to accelerate progress, improve safety, security and trust in AI, and maximize benefits to people and society everywhere. Members of the AI Alliance believe that open innovation is essential to develop and achieve safe and responsible AI that benefit society rather than benefit a select few big players.

description:
Join us for a webinar with DSR, a member of LF Decentralized Trust, on *Hiero: an ACA-Py plugin for the Hedera ledger*. Until recently, ACA-Py primarily relied on Hyperledger Indy as its verifiable data registry (VDR) for AnonCreds, but in 2025, Hedera emerged as a stable, enterprise-ready alternative. This session will introduce the LFDT Hiero project and demonstrate how the plugin enables credential issuance and verification using Hedera as a VDR within ACA-Py. We'll also explore the benefits of Hedera’s support for diverse credentials and protocols, making it easier to build SSI systems beyond the Indy ecosystem. The session is especially relevant for teams exploring alternatives to Indy or considering Hedera for identity use cases.

title: [AI Alliance] Improving Chatbot Reliability Through Graph-Based Retrieval
description:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a powerful technique for building chatbots that answer questions using your own content, but it can struggle with context and accuracy on complex sites. In this session, we demonstrate how integrating GraphRAG into the open-source AllyCat chatbot leads to more accurate and context-aware responses by leveraging graph-based retrieval.

With the addition of GraphRAG, this chat delivers more consistent and reliable answers, reducing hallucinations and improving the quality of chatbot interactions—key requirements for effective customer support, documentation, and user engagement.

This talk will include a live demo and code walkthrough, showing how developers can quickly integrate this with their own applications and adapt it to meet specific needs. By using AllyCat, developers can provide instant, accurate support to users and continuously improve their services.

**About the speaker**
Nyah Macklin is a Senior Developer Advocate at Neo4j, specializing in GraphRAG, knowledge graphs, and AI-driven developer tooling. An internationally recognized speaker, content creator, and advocate for ethical AI governance, Nyah has built high-impact technical communities and led initiatives that advance a critical understanding of AI and its use cases. They are also the Founder & CTO of Afros in AI, a technical community dedicated to showcasing the multifaceted nature of artificial intelligence. Beyond Nyah's technical expertise, Nyah has a background in government leadership and technology policy, having served as Chief of Staff in the U.S. state government, where they helped shape tech-driven legislative initiatives and equity-driven legislation. When not immersed in their work, Nyah cares about empowering, teaching, and tutoring engineers, live-streaming technical deep dives, and building open-source tools that make software more accessible, explainable, and community-driven.

description:
**🔐 Securing Digital Content + C2PA: How to Protect and Prove Content Integrity**
As digital video ecosystems grow in complexity, the need for strong, layered security becomes non-negotiable. In this online meetup, we’ll explore two key pillars of secure content workflows: **Encryption + DRM**, and **C2PA for content provenance**.

**Session 1: "Securing Digital Content: Key Management, DRM vs. Encryption, and Key Rotation"**
👤 *[David Eisenbacher](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-eisenbacher-276a75a1?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAABWxYjoBuwk_8OpJ0s4kvkQaHKfmc7FYx5s&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_search_srp_all%3Bi6wUhGpATV2EZ3gHSJlbRA%3D%3D)* – CEO EZDRM
This session offers a deep-dive into the foundations of content protection:

* **What encryption really protects** and how it's different from access control
* **How DRM and encryption complement each other** to manage user access and enforce business rules
* **Key rotation**: what it is, why it matters, and how it reduces the risk of long-term key exposure
* Common pitfalls and operational challenges in securing video at scale (multi-CDN delivery, latency, interoperability)
* How to build a secure and maintainable key management strategy

Whether you're protecting VOD, live content, or hybrid models, this session will empower you with the concepts and tactics you need to make informed decisions.

**Session 2: "Who said this? A look into C2PA and content provenance"**
👤 *[Fabián Cancela](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fcancela?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAACKv-s0BnbTOAYePf7D6_HvOFe4bq9TWlCc&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_search_srp_all%3Bxi5hWfFMQzS9qg2M8sayjw%3D%3D)* – Media Solutions Manager Qualabs
From fake content to AI-generated media, verifying the origin of digital assets is becoming a must-have.
This session breaks down how **C2PA** enables a **cryptographically verifiable chain of custody** for any digital asset.
You’ll learn:

* Key concepts in the C2PA spec: *claim, assertion, signature, provenance store*
* **The end-to-end lifecycle:** *capture → sign → package → distribute → verify*
* How it applies to **live streaming** with HLS and DASH (anchor-point and per-segment manifests)
* A **live demo** of asset signing and verification in-browser
* What to consider when integrating provenance in production workflows

🕔 **Time:** 5:00 p.m. UTC-3 / 4:00 p.m. EDT
Moderated by [Nicolas Levy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicolaslevylinares?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afs_miniProfile%3AACoAAAI69JoB3Yso2qT_I5L2UwqhPaVuMGYX-34&lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_search_srp_all%3BDHWInf4xS5K5bQb3O0XHOA%3D%3D)

title: [AI Alliance] How can Agents be Trusted?
description:
**The Landscape of AI Agents and Identity**

As AI agents grow more autonomous and pervasive—powering workflows, interfacing with users, and making decisions—the question of trust becomes unavoidable. Who are these agents acting on behalf of? What gives them the authority to act? How can we verify their provenance, their integrity, or even revoke that authority when needed?

This presentation explores the evolving landscape of AI Agents and Identity, highlighting the foundational challenges in building trusted agents. We’ll examine:

* Why traditional identity systems fall short in agent-based architectures
* The importance of verifiable identity, delegation, and auditability
* How to ensure agents are acting within their intended boundaries
* Emerging standards and design patterns that aim to make AI agent ecosystems secure, interoperable, and trustworthy
* Whether you're building agentic infrastructure or considering how identity fits into your AI strategy, this is a critical moment to shape the rules of trust.

**About the speaker**
Andor Kesselman is an engineer, builder, CTO, and open source advocate. He is currently the founder of a stealth startup building trust infrastructure for enterprise AI.

title: [AI Alliance] Better Expert Agents with Dana, Agent-Native Programming Language
description:
Every AI agent you build eventually hits the same walls: async complexity, brittle orchestration frameworks, and data that can't leave your infrastructure. What if you could build expert AI agents entirely on your laptop, without sending a single byte to the cloud?This session introduces Dana, a local-first agent programming language designed for building AI agents. Get a working expert agent in minutes:

* Long running, multi-step agent workflows on a single line: `step1 | step2 | [step3a, step3b, step3c] | step4`
* Built-in concurrency for parallel LLM calls with zero async keywords
* Deterministic execution with learning loops that improve reliability over time

Whether you're dealing with sensitive data, air-gapped requirements, or cloud API limitations—come see what agent development looks like when everything runs locally.

title: 🧉 Mate Talk: "Challenges in Standardizing New Video Ad Formats"
description:
Join us for the next MateTalk, our relaxed, roundtable-style meetup where industry experts and community members dive deep into timely topics in video tech!

We’re excited to welcome **[Katie Stroud](https://www.linkedin.com/in/katiestroud/)** from **[IAB Tech Lab](https://www.linkedin.com/company/iabtechlab/)** as our special guest, alongside our fixed panel: **Alex Zambelli, Connie Huang, David Hassoun, Peter Scott** and **JP Saibene**.

This session will be an open, collaborative discussion on the challenges and opportunities of **standardizing new formats for video advertising**, including:

* Why nonlinear ad formats (L-bars, squeezebacks, overlays, etc.) bring both innovation potential and technical complexity.
* The difficulty of ensuring predictable behavior across diverse players and platforms.
* How open standards and reference implementations could drive broader adoption.
* Why the advertising industry has been slow to adopt surround/immersive audio, 4K, HDR, multilingual audio and subtitles — and how ad mezzanine quality still lags behind regular content by 10–15 years.
* Opportunities in metadata, signaling, and measurement to support interoperability.

True to the MateTalk spirit, this will be an **open, multi-angle conversation** that spans technology, product, and business perspectives — shaped by your questions and insights.

title: Agent-to-Agent Interactions with NLIP and an application to AllyCat
description:
**Description**
NLIP (Natural Language Interaction Protocol) is a project defining an interoperable protocol for user-to-agent and agent-to-agent natural language interactions. In this talk, Tom will describe the goals of the NLIP project and then demonstrate a proof of concept agent network built using NLIP. One of the agents is an AllyCat instance that has been modified by giving it an NLIP server. By adding NLIP to the AllyCat server, it is immediately available to Chat Clients and other Agents, making it part of an expanding network of agents.

**Speaker bio**

Tom Sheffler is a computer engineer currently working towards interoperability of secure agentic systems. He is also a solution architect with UnifabriX - a maker of CXL memory pooling systems for memory-bound HPC applications. Previously, Tom built global web applications for managing and scaling genomics computations at Roche. As an entrepreneur, he founded the cloud-based video analytics company, Sensr.net, that provided a consumer solution for home security cameras. Tom was an early employee at Rambus where he worked on the architecture and verification of high-speed memory devices.

title: [AI Alliance] How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
description:
LLM-based web agents have recently made significant progress, but much of it has occurred in closed-source systems, widening the gap with open-source alternatives. Progress has been held back by two key challenges: first, a narrow focus on single-step tasks that overlooks the complexity of multi-step web interactions; and second, the high compute costs required to post-train LLM-based web agents.

To address this, we present the first statistically grounded study on compute allocation for LLM web-agent post-training. Our approach uses a two-stage pipeline, training a Llama 3.1 8B or QWEN 2.5 7B student to imitate a Llama 3.3 70B teacher or QWEN 2.5 72B via supervised fine-tuning (SFT), followed by on-policy reinforcement learning (GRPO).

We find this process highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices, making exhaustive sweeps impractical. To spare others from expensive trial-and-error, we sample 1,370 configurations and use bootstrapping to estimate effective hyperparameters. Our results show that combining SFT with on-policy RL consistently outperforms either approach alone on both WorkArena and MiniWob++. Further, this strategy requires only 55% of the compute to match the peak performance of pure SFT on MiniWob++, effectively pushing the compute-performance Pareto frontier, and is the only strategy that can close the gap with closed-source models.

Read the paper on ArXiv: [How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.04103) (PDF)

**About the speaker**

I’m Massimo Caccia, Senior Research Scientist at [ServiceNow Research](https://www.servicenow.com/research/), specializing in post-training methods for computer-use agents. I see computer use as the ultimate playground for testing agents, thanks to its ubiquity and diversity. My research involves conducting large-scale empirical studies to systematically evaluate trade-offs among different approaches and to develop practical know-how, with reinforcement learning being a particular focus.

As a core contributor to the web-agent research library ecosystem, I actively shape evaluation frameworks ([BrowserGym](https://github.com/ServiceNow/BrowserGym), [WorkArena](https://github.com/ServiceNow/WorkArena)) and development platforms ([AgentLab](https://github.com/ServiceNow/AgentLab)). My goal is to bridge foundational research and scalable tools to advance the field.

Previously, I completed my Ph.D. at the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute ([Mila](https://mila.quebec/en/)) under Professor [Laurent Charlin](http://www.cs.toronto.edu/~lcharlin/). During my doctoral studies, I collaborated with [DeepMind](https://deepmind.com/)’s Continual Learning team led by [Marc’Aurelio Ranzato](https://ranzato.github.io/), [Amazon](https://www.amazon.science/)’s team under [Alex Smola](https://alex.smola.org/), and ElementAI prior to its integration with ServiceNow.

My Ph.D. research focused on building agents capable of accumulating and transferring knowledge across tasks, drawing from continual learning, transfer learning, and meta-learning. My work explored applications in language, vision, and reinforcement learning, emphasizing improvements in data and compute efficiency.

The [AI Alliance](https://thealliance.ai) is an international community of researchers, developers and organizational leaders committed to support and enhance open innovation across the AI technology landscape to accelerate progress, improve safety, security and trust in AI, and maximize benefits to people and society everywhere. Members of the AI Alliance believe that open innovation is essential to develop and achieve safe and responsible AI that benefit society rather than benefit a select few big players.

title: Making Zero-Knowledge Smart Contract Development Accessible, Secure & Practical
description:
Join us for a virtual meetup about Minokawa, the newest project hosted by LF Decentralized Trust. [Minokawa joins the LFDT project ecosystem as an established codebase and with an existing user base](https://www.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/blog/compact-smart-contract-language-is-now-minokawa-newest-lf-decentralized-trust-project). It was designed under the Compact brand with a clear set of goals: to make zero-knowledge smart contract development accessible, secure, and practical for real-world applications. Compact’s features and capabilities are now at the core of Minokawa. They include:

\* Privacy by default
\* Strong static typing
\* Zero-Knowledge proof integration
\* Separation of public and private state
\* Developer accessibility

At its core, Minokawa addresses the structural limitations that have historically constrained the development of private, trustworthy smart contracts. On most blockchains, both contract state and logic are fully transparent, which makes them rather unsuitable for applications that involve sensitive information, such as credentials, personal identity, private preferences, or proprietary business logic.

Join us for this event to learn more about Minokawa and how to get involved in the project.

**Speaker**

title: [AI Alliance] Connect On-prem Solutions via NLIP
description:
This use case showcases how Natural Language Interaction Protocol (NLIP) could facilitate the integration of on-premises resources such as Active Directory with cloud providers such as ServiceNow. Special attention is paid to moderation of communications for signs of jailbreaking, etc. to combat some regular problems.

**About the presenter**

**Will Witten** is a pragmatic builder and customer educator focused on AI that actually ships and sticks. He specializes in translating plain-English requests into production-grade workflows, stress-testing designs to expose brittle spots before they reach users. A strong advocate for the **Natural Language Interaction Protocol (NLIP)**, he treats it as a practical bridge—standardizing how systems converse while leaving room for each side’s constraints so results don’t break on contact with reality. Today he will share about his experience working with Natural Language Interaction Protocol, the latest standard for dependable natural language interactions, including a real-world example to demonstrate how this standard can benefit you. (edited)

The [AI Alliance](https://thealliance.ai) is an international community of researchers, developers and organizational leaders committed to support and enhance open innovation across the AI technology landscape to accelerate progress, improve safety, security and trust in AI, and maximize benefits to people and society everywhere. title: Configuración, Despliegue y Gestión de una Red Privada Besu
description:
[Besu](https://github.com/hyperledger/besu), un proyecto de LF Decentralized Trust, es un cliente Ethereum de código abierto desarrollado bajo la licencia Apache 2.0 e implementado en Java. En este taller, aprenderás los conceptos básicos de las características de Besu y cómo operar y gestionar una red privada. A través de cuatro ejercicios prácticos, adquirirás experiencia práctica en la implementación, actualización, uso y supervisión de una red privada Besu.

El objetivo principal de este taller es proporcionar una comprensión integral de los aspectos teóricos y prácticos de Besu. Está diseñado para personas familiarizadas con la tecnología blockchain y el protocolo Ethereum. Si está buscando un punto de partida sólido para convertirse en un profesional certificado por Besu, este taller gratuito debería estar en su agenda.

Para participar en este taller, debe tener lo siguiente:

* 1\. Un sistema operativo Linux para ejecutar scripts bash\.
* 2\. Software instalado: Metamask\, Docker y Docker Compose\.
* 3\. El repositorio de código abierto del taller\, que se puede descargar desde: [https://gitlab.com/iobuilders-public/iob-besu-workshop](https://gitlab.com/iobuilders-public/iob-besu-workshop).

title: Cross-Network Interoperability with Hyperledger Cacti Workshop
description:
In this workshop, participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of the [Hyperledger Cacti project](https://github.com/hyperledger-cacti/cacti)—its current state, opportunities for contribution, and the end-to-end solutions it enables, with a special focus on the Secure Asset Transfer Protocol (SATP), soon to be an IETF standard. We will discuss how developers can contribute and extend the project by creating new plugins and connectors for unsupported distributed ledger technologies (DLTs). We will also showcase, use, and enhance existing end-to-end solutions already available within Hyperledger Cacti with SATP-based solutions as example use cases.

**Key Topics Covered**

* Introduction to Interoperability & Hyperledger Cacti: Brief overview of interoperability concepts, Cacti’s purpose, functionality, and modular architecture. We will refer the audience to previous workshops that delve into these topics.
* Integrated Multi-Modal Architecture: What has been achieved, ongoing work, and future directions.
* Building a Plugin From Scratch: Step-by-step walkthrough on creating a new connector for unsupported ledgers.
* Secure Asset Transfer Protocol (SATP): Introduction to IETF’s SATP, its design, operating model, and role in trust-minimized cross-network transfers.
* Demonstration of Asset Transfer Implementations in Cacti: Practical demonstrations will showcase asset transfers using Hyperledger Cacti end-to-end solutions. Participants will observe the solutions available in Hyperledger Cacti in action and gain hands-on experience in executing cross-network asset transfers.

**Target Audience**

The workshop is meant for developers, blockchain enthusiasts, and enterprise stakeholders who want to enhance their knowledge of DLT interoperability and standardized asset transfer protocols. While prior experience with blockchain fundamentals and some familiarity with Hyperledger Cacti can be helpful, it is not a strict requirement.

**Speakers**
[Carlos Amaro](https://www.linkedin.com/in/carlos-amaro-1284b020a/), Ph.D. Student
[André Augusto](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreaaugusto/), Ph.D. Candidate and Blockchain Researcher
[Venkatraman Ramakrishna](https://research.ibm.com/people/venkatraman-ramakrishna), Senior Researcher at IBM
[Weijia Zhang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/weijia-zhang-013b84153/), Vice President of Engineering at Wanchain

title: [AI Alliance] Gofannon: Ramen
description:
Everyone is talking about agents; if you don't have agents already in production you are hopelessly behind. Wasn't vibe coding supposed to take care of everyone's computer problems? How am I behind if AI takes care of everything for me now? Maybe I need an MCP and then I'll be caught up. Wouldn't it be nice if there was a tool where I could just say what I wanted the agent to do and it would vibe it out for me? And then maybe I could tell it what I wanted the app to look like, and it would vibe that out too. That day is today, that tool is called gofannon.

In this talk we'll discuss our motivations for making gofannon, lessons learned that we've incorporated from prior iterations, and a (possibly live) demo where we'll go from idea to deployed app. See you there!

Trevor Grant (IBM)
