title: Summer Camp 2026 | Kick-off: The Open Source AI Co-Pilot for Media Archives
description:
Join us for the kickoff of **AI Co-Pilot for Media Archives**, one of the open-source projects of **[Summer Camp 2026](https://montevideotech.dev/summercamp2026/)**!

This session will introduce the **vision, objectives, and collaboration plan,** exploring how AI and RAG strategies can help media organizations (like [SMPTE](https://www.smpte.org/) and its partners) make sense of the massive, fragmented archives they’ve built over time.

**The problem**
Across the media industry, archives are rarely a single, unified collection. They’re a mix of data scattered across multiple formats and systems: PDFs, videos, images, audio, Word documents, meeting notes, webinars, and more. For organizations like SMPTE, this diversity makes it increasingly difficult to find, connect, and reuse valuable knowledge.

🎯 **The goal**
To build an **AI-powered assistant** that can search and interpret these **diverse data sources**, understand relationships between them, and provide contextual answers — while laying the groundwork for future provenance and access-control capabilities.

👥 **Tech Sponsor:** Andy Beach (Think Alchemy)
**Summer** **Project Leads:** Nicolás Levy and Fabián Cancela

Whether you’re passionate about AI, knowledge graphs, or media-tech innovation, join us to discover how this project aims to redefine the way the SMPTE community, and the broader industry, explores its archives.

Let’s build the **AI Co-Pilot that will help unlock the archives** of the future.

title: Decentralized Directory (DeDi)—Infrastructure, Use Cases & Architecture

Join us for an exploratory session into **[DeDi](https://dedi.global/)** — the decentralized trust infrastructure redefining how public data and registries are shared, verified, and consumed in the digital age.

**What to expect**
We’ll dig into:
**1\. Introduction to DeDi** (Speaker: Amar Tumballi)
\* The story behind DeDi: origin, mission, and positioning
\* Real-life deployment use cases
\* How to evaluate new opportunities for applying DeDi in your organization
**2\. Architecture of DeDi** (Speaker: Mudit Sarda)
\* The internal design and deployment modes of DeDi
\* How scale, performance, and security are handled
\* Areas open to contribution, improvement, and extension
We’ll wrap with a Q&A and open discussion: how DeDi could be leveraged in domains you care about (govtech, fintech, identity, compliance, etc.).
**Resources**
\* DeDi’s site: Decentralized Directory for public registries ([https://www.dedi.global/](https://www.dedi.global/))
\* GitHub / technical spec: Finternet / DeDi ([https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/DeDi](https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/DeDi))
\* DeDi publish interface: publish.dedi.global ([https://publish.dedi.global/](https://publish.dedi.global/))
**Why Attend**
\* Understand a next-generation \*\*Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)\*\* building block
\* Learn how cryptographic trust\, revocation propagation\, cross\-registry recognition\, and verifiability are being solved end\-to\-end via DeDi \(\[dedi\.global\]\[1\]\)
\* Gain insight into how your organization can plug into or extend the DeDi ecosystem
\* Network with peers, architects, and early adopters in the trust & infrastructure space
**Who Should Join**
\* Software architects, system engineers, infrastructure leads
\* Product leads / innovation teams in governments, NGOs, fintech, identity technology
\* Researchers and technologists interested in trust, verifiable systems, decentralized infrastructure
\* Anyone curious about the foundations of public data infrastructure
**Agenda (Tentative)**
\| 0–10 min \| Welcome\, overview & framing \|
\| 10–40 min \| “Introduction to DeDi” by Amar Tumballi \|
\| 40–70 min \| “Architecture of DeDi” by Mudit Sarda \|
\| 70–90 min \| Q&A \+ open discussion \+ next steps

title: Fabric-X-Orderer Overview: A Scalable BFT Ordering Service for Fabric-X
description:
[Fabric-X is a digital asset-specific implementation of Hyperledger Fabric](https://www.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/blog/new-major-contribution-to-hyperledger-fabric-purpose-built-implementation-for-next-gen-digital-assets). Join us for a series on meetups that go into detail about what Fabric-X is and how you can use it.

Fabric-X-Orderer is the new ordering service designed for [Fabric-X](https://github.com/hyperledger/fabric-x), built on a scalable Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) consensus protocol named **Arma**. Arma introduces key architectural innovations to support high transaction throughput, including the separation of consensus from transaction dissemination, and the use of **sharding** and **pipelining** to enhance parallelism in transaction processing. These techniques enable Arma to achieve over **100,000 transactions per second (TPS)** for small transactions, meeting the performance targets of Fabric-X.

In this meetup, we will provide an overview of the Fabric-X-Orderer architecture, delve into the underlying protocols, and share performance evaluation results that highlight its scalability and efficiency.

**Join us for the other Fabric-X meetups**

* October 21: [Fabric-X – Programming Model and Application Development Deep Dive](https://www.meetup.com/lfdt-sf/events/310510064/)
* December 9: [Fabric-X-Committer: A Microservices-Based Committer Architecture for Ultra-High Throughput](https://www.meetup.com/lfdt-sf/events/310510523/)

**Speaker**

Adam Pingel ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adampingel/), [GitHub](https://github.com/adampingel)) is IBM's Head of Open Tools and Applications for the [AI Alliance](https://thealliance.ai). Adam has been fascinated by AI and chatbots since playing with [Racter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racter) in the 80’s. But the “winters” were long and frequent. title: Fabric-X-Committer: A Microservices-Based Architecture for Ultra-High Throughput
description:
[Fabric-X is a digital asset-specific implementation of Hyperledger Fabric](https://www.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/blog/new-major-contribution-to-hyperledger-fabric-purpose-built-implementation-for-next-gen-digital-assets). Join us for a series on meetups that go into detail about what Fabric-X is and how you can use it.

[Fabric-X-Committer](https://github.com/hyperledger/fabric-x-committer) introduces a high-performance and resilient architecture that addresses the scalability limitations of the traditional monolithic peer in Fabric. By decomposing the commit process into independently scalable microservices—including a Coordinator, Signature Verifiers, and Validator-Committers and leveraging a sharded distributed database, the system achieves significant parallelism, enabling substantial scalability and performance gains.

A key innovation is the use of a transaction dependency graph, which allows safe, parallel validation of transactions across multiple blocks. Combined with a pipelined execution flow, this design eliminates sequential bottlenecks and unlocks ultra-high throughput. Performance evaluations show that Fabric-X-Committer can process over 200,000 transactions per second, marking a major leap in scalability for enterprise-grade blockchain systems.

In this meetup, we will provide an overview of the Fabric-X-Committer architecture and share performance evaluation results that highlight its scalability and efficiency.

**Join us for the other Fabric-X meetups**

* October 21: [Fabric-X – Programming Model and Application Development Deep Dive](https://www.meetup.com/lfdt-sf/events/310510064/)
* November 19: [Fabric-X-Orderer Overview: A Scalable BFT Ordering Service for Fabric-X](https://www.meetup.com/lfdt-sf/events/310510263/)

SwissLedger is a Swiss institutional blockchain designed for regulated use cases across banking, industry and public administration. It evolved from Lugano’s city-level blockchain initiatives into a national-scale infrastructure, with governance, security and compliance built in by design.

In this session, Lorenzo will outline SwissLedger’s public-permissioned Proof of Authority (PoA) model, consortium governance and compliance-ready architecture. title: AIA: An Open-Source Semantic Framework for Universally Interpretable Impact Data
description:
Climate and sustainability projects generate vast amounts of impact data — but too often, that data is hard to compare, integrate, or audit. Different projects use different terms, schemas, and structures — even when they are measuring the same underlying phenomena. This fragmentation creates friction for integrators and limits meaningful, global, cross-platform impact accounting.

On 17 February 2026 at 08:00 AM Pacific, the LFDT CA2-SIG Standards Working Group will present the [Anthropogenic Impact Accounting (AIA) ontology suite](https://www.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/blog/climate-action-official-release-of-the-anthropogenic-impact-accounting-ontology-suite), an open-source semantic framework designed to address this challenge. Developed over four years through rigorous bi-weekly working sessions and multiple redrafting cycles, the AIA suite provides a coherent and extensible foundation for expressing impact data in a universally interpretable way.

The first public release of AIA, published on 16 September 2025, comprises four modular, W3ID-registered ontologies:
\- claimont \([https://w3id.org/claimont](https://w3id.org/claimont)): Semantics for claims, claimants, evidence, and attestations
\- infocomm \([https://w3id.org/infocomm](https://w3id.org/infocomm)): Communication primitives for structured information exchange
\- impactont \([https://w3id.org/impactont](https://w3id.org/impactont)): Foundational concepts for modeling impact relationships
\- aiao \([https://w3id.org/aiao](https://w3id.org/aiao)): An integrated framework for anthropogenic impact accounting

Join us for an overview of how AIA can help your impact data become more interoperable, auditable, and reusable!

title: Workshop: CREDEBL For Decentralized Identity and Verifiable Credentials
description:
As adoption of Decentralized Identity (DID) and Verifiable Credentials (VCs) accelerates across governments, education, enterprises, and regulated industries, developers and organizations need open, interoperable, and production-ready infrastructure to build trusted digital ecosystems.

This webinar introduces [CREDEBL](https://github.com/credebl/), an LF Decentralized Trust project, and walks participants through how to get started quickly, understand the architecture, and explore real-world use cases - all backed by open standards and community-driven development.

Whether you are a developer, architect, policy stakeholder, system integrator, or ecosystem partner, this session will help you move from concepts to implementation.

**What We’ll Cover**

* The Problem: Fragmented Digital Trust : Why identity, credentials, and verification remain siloed - and how this limits interoperability, privacy, and adoption.
* The Foundation: Verifiable Credentials & Decentralized Identity : A brief overview of DIDs, VCs, DIDComm, OID4VC, trust frameworks and where CREDEBL fits within the LFDT ecosystem.
* The Platform: CREDEBL Architecture : Core components, issuer–holder–verifier flows, APIs, and deployment models.
* Getting Started Fast: One-Click / Minimal-Config Setup : Live walkthrough of setting up CREDEBL and running end-to-end credential flows.
* Live Demo: Issuance & Verification in Action : Creating DIDs, issuing credentials, wallet interactions, and verification scenarios.
* Real-World Adoption & Ecosystem Use Cases : Education, digital identity, enterprise and public-sector use cases.
* Community, Governance & Roadmap : Open-source contribution model, roadmap, and how to get involved with the CREDEBL and LFDT community.

title: Trusted AI Agents by Design: From Trust Ecosystems to Authority Continuity
description:
Rapid innovation in agentic AI is opening up real potential. But agents don't just forward intent, they create it. When an agent makes the decisions that matter, trust can't be assumed, it has to be designed in. And once agents cross organizational boundaries, decentralized trust infrastructure has a critical role to play.

This session brings together two complementary pieces tackling that fundamental challenge, followed by a panel. This is the timeframe to get things right. Join us.

**5:00 PM Opening & Framing** – Shane Deconinck

**5:10 PM Running AI Agent Protocols over Trust Spanning Protocol** – Wenjing Chu
How TMCP and TA2A bring secure, interoperable communication to AI agent ecosystems, built on the Trust Spanning Protocol.

**5:35 PM Authority Is Continuous** – Nicola Gallo
Introducing PIC (Provenance Identity Continuity Protocol) and its Proof of Continuity as an emerging security primitive for distributed transactions and agent chains.

**6:00 PM Closing Panel: Connecting the Layers** – Moderated by Shane Deconinck
We'll discuss how the proposed solutions fit together, which pieces are still missing, how they align with existing standards and ongoing work in the space, and what's needed to move from specification to adoption, with plenty of room for interaction.

**Learn more:**
[TSP: Strengthening Trust in Human and AI Interactions (PDF)](https://trustoverip.org/wp-content/uploads/TSP_-Strengthening-Trust-in-Human-and-AI-Interactions.pdf)
[PIC Protocol](https://www.pic-protocol.org/)

This session will open the discussion around where the industry is heading.

Speakers:

* Andrew Freeman @ Baylor University
**“MOQ to the Future: Client-Side Video Analysis for Distributed Content Moderation"**

Andrew will present a distributed architecture leveraging the Media Over QUIC Transport protocol to enable client-side content analysis and filtering, adding latency only for users who enable content filters. His session will cover propagation bounds, failure handling, analyzer selection, security considerations, and prototype feasibility in practical MoQ-based systems.

* James Hynard @ Castlabs
**"Soft Binding in C2PA: Limitations, opportunities, and the role of Watermarking"**

James will present the current state of C2PA, its technical limitations, and the concept of soft binding. He’ll also discuss how watermarking can help address existing weaknesses and where this technology may extend beyond its original scope.

We’re excited to get back into the conversation and reconnect with the community for a new year of technical exchanges.

title: IA: Cómo modernizar tus modelos de datos con Databricks Agéntico con Databricks
description:
En esta edición exploraremos **IA: Cómo modernizar tus modelos de datos con Databricks**, aplicando un enfoque acelerado basado en herramientas nativas del ecosistema. Veremos cómo **modernizar la gobernanza de datos**, migrar modelos legacy a Databricks y sentar una base confiable para **construir agentes de IA** sobre datos gobernados.

Durante la **primera charla** presentaremos nuestro **Databricks Governance Accelerator**, diseñado para ayudar a las organizaciones a trasladar sus modelos de gobernanza existentes hacia Databricks de forma estructurada y escalable. Mostraremos cómo el acelerador utiliza capacidades como Lakebase, Databricks Apps y AgentBricks para automatizar la definición de políticas, gestionar metadatos, organizar dominios de datos y facilitar la adopción de buenas prácticas de gobierno dentro de la plataforma.
Una vez que existe una base sólida de gobernanza y datos bien organizados, se abre la puerta a nuevas formas de interacción con la información.

En la **segunda charla** exploraremos el **mundo agéntico y cómo Databricks está habilitando nuevas formas de productividad mediante AI Agents**. Veremos cómo los agentes pueden integrarse con la plataforma de datos para automatizar tareas, asistir a los equipos en sus workflows y facilitar el acceso al conocimiento dentro de las organizaciones.
La sesión combinará arquitectura, ejemplos prácticos y recomendaciones de implementación para equipos que estén construyendo plataformas modernas de datos y analítica sobre Databricks.

**🔹 ¿A quién está dirigido?**

🎯 Data Engineers & Architects
🎯 Data Scientists & Analysts
🎯 Empresas y startups que usan Databricks
🎯 Profesionales interesados en Big Data e Inteligencia Artificial

**👨‍💼 Speakers**

**Douglas Silva\| Solutions Architect Latam**
Especialista en IA Generativa, datos y nube, con más de 10 años de experiencia ayudando a empresas a impulsar la innovación, acelerar la transformación digital y generar resultados de negocio mediante soluciones tecnológicas de alto impacto.

**Marco Luquer \| Solution Engineer / Databricks Champion**
Enfocado en Generative AI, LLMs y pipelines de datos de nivel productivo sobre Databricks Lakehouse, Marco trabaja junto a equipos de producto y data para definir casos de uso, diseñar arquitecturas escalables y generar resultados medibles.

**Facundo Sentena Tejera \| Senior AI Engineer**
Senior AI Engineer en Qubika, enfocado en diseñar, desarrollar y desplegar aplicaciones de GenAI robustas y escalables, incluyendo sistemas de Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) adaptados a necesidades de negocio. Entrega soluciones end to end, desde el diseño y la orquestación de prompts hasta el despliegue y monitoreo, y contribuye a crear frameworks reutilizables que aceleran la entrega de IA dentro del Studio. Es Databricks Certified Data Analyst Associate.

title: Briolette: An Experimental Framework For Offline-First Currency
description:
Briolette ([https://github.com/Briolette](https://github.com/Briolette)) is an opinionated digital currency framework that provides a foundation for digital currency designers, whether centralized or decentralized. It enables offline and online peer-to-peer transactions with cryptographically-backed double spend detection and abuse resistance mechanisms. Briolette is built around direct anonymous attestation primitives which enable pseudonymous, transaction-based identities and complex system-wide policy tooling. title: O Futuro das Tecnologias Descentralizadas e o Protagonismo Brasileiro
description:
O Capítulo Brasil da Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT) convida toda a comunidade tecnológica, desenvolvedores, entusiastas e tomadores de decisão para um encontro exclusivo com a liderança global da fundação.

Neste evento online e gratuito, discutiremos a evolução do ecossistema de confiança descentralizada. A LFDT vai além do Blockchain, englobando uma governança robusta para soluções de identidade digital, criptografia e infraestrutura de código aberto que fundamentam a economia digital moderna.

O que vamos abordar:

* Visão Global e Governança: Como a LFDT gerencia projetos críticos como Hyperledger Besu, Fabric, frentes de identidade digital entre outras soluções de código aberto para criação de redes de confiança decentralizada como é o modelo Web3.
* O Brasil como Protagonista: O país deixou de ser apenas um usuário de tecnologia para se tornar um ator relevante na contribuição e desenvolvimento do ecossistema global.
* Código Aberto vs. Lock-in Tecnológico: Por que o open source é a estratégia fundamental para países em desenvolvimento garantirem soberania digital e mitigarem a dependência de fornecedores únicos.
* Desafios e Oportunidades: As perspectivas da fundação para o próximo ano e onde estão as maiores janelas de inovação para profissionais e empresas brasileiras.

Este é um espaço aberto para troca de conhecimento, networking e para entender como você ou sua organização podem contribuir ativamente com a Linux Foundation.

## Apresentação da Palestrante

**Daniela Barbosa Diretora Executiva da Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT)**

Daniela Barbosa é uma líder global no setor de tecnologia, com vasta experiência em ecossistemas de código aberto e inovação em enterprise blockchain. À frente da LFDT, ela coordena o desenvolvimento de padrões e tecnologias que sustentam a confiança digital em escala global. Com um olhar estratégico sobre a colaboração comunitária, Daniela tem sido uma ponte fundamental entre as demandas das grandes indústrias e a agilidade das comunidades de desenvolvedores, defendendo sempre o impacto positivo das tecnologias descentralizadas no crescimento econômico e na inclusão digital.

**Hart Montgomery, Diretor de Tecnologia da Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT)**

Hart possui vasta experiência em blockchain e criptografia, tendo atuado anteriormente em pesquisa nessas áreas na Fujitsu Research, onde ajudou a liderar os esforços da Fujitsu no Hyperledger. Antes da Fujitsu, Hart obteve seu doutorado em criptografia na Universidade de Stanford, sob a orientação de Dan Boneh, período em que foi bolsista de pós-graduação da instituição (Stanford Graduate Fellow). Hart conta com inúmeras publicações acadêmicas e patentes nas áreas de criptografia e blockchain, trazendo uma vasta experiência nesses domínios para a LF Decentralized Trust.

## Informações Gerais

* Público-alvo: Desenvolvedores de software, arquitetos de sistemas, gestores de TI, pesquisadores acadêmicos, estudantes, empreendedores do setor de tecnologia e qualquer pessoa interessada em Blockchain, Criptografia e Identidade Digital.

title: From Identity-First to Authority Continuity
description:
We built security around identity, tokens, and roles. It was never quite right, capability theorists knew this decades ago. AI agents just made the cracks impossible to ignore.

This is the moment to correct the model.

We will reason from first principles. What identity is. What an identifier is. What authority actually is, not a token you hold, but a continuous property of execution that can only shrink, never expand. Why confused deputy and privilege escalation are not edge cases. They are the structural outcome of building on possession.

We will work through the real delegation cases that break every IAM system built today, defined by Alan Karp, who has spent decades mapping them. Delegation and attenuation. Chained delegation across organizations. Revocation, including the hard case where you need to revoke someone you never delegated to directly. The confused deputy, known since 1988, still appearing in every generation of systems. Seven aspects of sharing that people rely on in the real world and that no identity-based, role-based, or attribute-based system handles correctly. The use cases are here: [alanhkarp.com/UseCases.pdf](http://alanhkarp.com/UseCases.pdf)

We will then explore how authority continuity changes everything. Moving from identity-first to an intent and execution model means authority is anchored at the origin, flows through a verifiable chain, and cannot be expanded, stolen, or reinterpreted at any hop.

AI agents are the opportunity we did not expect. Authority continuity is the correction we always needed.

title: Open Standards for Tokenization: Why Interoperability Matters
description:
Institutional adoption of tokenized assets depends on solving a critical infrastructure challenge: how can digital securities operate across multiple platforms, jurisdictions, and compliance regimes without recreating the vendor lock-in that has long limited legacy systems?

Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust and OpenAssets are helping establish this foundational layer through the Open Tokenized Asset Standard (OTAS), a recently approved lab focused on building protocol-agnostic standards for compliant, interoperable digital assets.

In this session, Surendra Kalidindi, CTO of OpenAssets, will start by exploring why open standards matter for institutional digital assets and how open approaches differ from proprietary tokenization platforms.

The session will be followed by a panel moderated by Daniela Barbosa, Executive Director of LF Decentralized Trust, featuring industry leaders from a global financial institution, a protocol engineering organization, and a provider of cross-chain and onchain data infrastructure. Together, they will discuss what the industry needs most to accelerate adoption, improve interoperability, and support real-world deployment at scale.

Join us to hear directly from industry leaders, learn more about initiatives like OTAS and the goals of the newly launched lab, and explore how institutions and developers can engage with the OTAS Lab, including a 2026 mentorship opportunity through LF Decentralized Trust.

**Please note: This event is being shared with our entire global community. If you're interested in this content but can't attend the event live, feel free to sign up and we will send you a link to the recording after the meetup is over.**

title: Meetup #18
description:
Te invitamos a la edición #18 de la meetup de ConnectIA!

En esta ocasión tendremos dos charlas: una sobre forecasting aplicado al pronóstico de demanda eléctrica en Uruguay (caso UTE), y una segunda charla a cargo de Sebastián Galli (próximamente compartimos detalles).
Al final tendremos comida y bebidas para compartir con el resto de los participantes y hacer networking con la comunidad.
Recuerda que también tenemos un espacio en Slack donde compartimos información y coordinamos actividades. Si aún no estás inscrito, puedes hacerlo aquí.
———————————————
📍 DIRECCIÓN
**Digital Sense** — Brenda 5751, esquina Motivos de Proteo, Montevideo.
———————————————
🗓️ AGENDA
6:30 PM — Recepción de invitad@s
7:00 PM — Inicio de la jornada + bienvenida del host
7:05 PM — Charla 1: Forecasting con intención
7:35 PM — Preguntas
7:50 PM — Charla 2: Sebastián Galli
8:20 PM — Preguntas
8:35 PM — Comida & Networking
9:30 PM — Cierre
———————————————
🎤 CHARLA 1
Forecasting con intención: Cerrando la brecha entre algoritmos complejos y el valor para el usuario a través de UTE
Speaker: Marcelo Martínez
Empresa: Digital Sense
Descripción:
Existe una gran variedad de modelos de forecasting: desde regresiones lineales simples hasta modelos de transformers y generativos. Ante el avance del aprendizaje automático (ML), puede ser tentador recurrir a los modelos más sofisticados. Sin embargo, probar distintas arquitecturas y optimizar hiperparámetros puede resultar solo en mejoras marginales.
En su lugar, comprender a fondo las necesidades del cliente y traducirlas en acciones concretas durante el desarrollo del modelo puede generar resultados superiores. A través del caso de estudio sobre el pronóstico de la demanda eléctrica en Uruguay, analizaremos cómo abordar un problema de predicción desde una perspectiva holística, con el objetivo de desarrollar un sistema que sea preciso en el papel pero, sobre todo, útil para sus usuarios.
———————————————
🎤 CHARLA 2
Cómo ejecutar un roadmap cuando el futuro cambia cada semana (IA)
Speaker: Sebastián Galli
Empresa: Delto
Descripción:
Esta charla explora el desafío de ejecutar un roadmap de producto en un contexto donde la inteligencia artificial avanza a una velocidad que invalida supuestos en cuestión de meses. A partir de preguntas concretas, se analizará cómo decisiones y features que parecían estratégicos hace seis meses pueden volverse obsoletos hoy, y qué implica esto para la planificación, priorización y ejecución de producto. El foco estará en cómo adaptarse a este cambio constante: cuándo mantener el rumbo, cuándo pivotear, y cómo construir roadmaps más flexibles, iterativos y resilientes frente a la incertidumbre tecnológica.
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sebastiangalli/
———————————————
Gracias Digital Sense por acompañarnos esta vez y hacer posible nuestro encuentro! 🙏

**¿Cómo participar?** Simplemente te registras al evento. Los cupos son limitados por capacidad del lugar. Si estás en lista de espera serás notificado cuando se liberen lugares.

**AVISO:** *OWASP UY dejará de usar la plataforma Meetup para eventos futuros. Usaremos [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/owasp-uruguay-chapter/), el [Google Group](https://groups.google.com/a/owasp.org/forum/#!forum/uruguay-chapter) hasta que se habilite un nuevo sitio web propio de OWASP para el registro a eventos, del cual se dará aviso.*

**Marcos Martínez, Tiago Zarzavidjian:** Secure development en la era de coding agents
*La idea es contar algunos problemas, buenas prácticas desde nuestro lado pero que sea también una forma de invitar a la conversación de todos.*

**Sebastián Passaro:** Testing para que mis agentes no hagan cualquiera
*Un sistema de agentes no solo produce texto: también actúa. Y cuando falla, no falla «una frase», falla una decisión y eso puede disparar efectos secundarios inesperados (aprobar, enviar, borrar, etiquetar).*
*En este espacio voy a salir de la abstracción y teoría para mostrar un caso de sistema de agentes que operan sobre emails, cómo pueden ser abusados con inyecciones de prompt indirectas, y cómo convertir ese riesgo en una suite de pruebas repetible usando Promptfoo: casos fijos, entradas controladas y evaluación directa de salidas de los agentes (acciones/traza), validando condiciones invariantes en un plano determinista aunque las respuestas varíen.*
*Todo esto entre una versión vulnerable y una versión corregida del mismo sistema. La idea es que te lleves algo valioso y aplicable en la práctica para tu laburo o proyecto personal.*

**¡Te esperamos!**

title: Hiero Heka: A Ready-To-Use Decentralized Identity Solution
description:
The Heka Identity Platform is a ready-to-use decentralized identity (aka Self-Sovereign Identity or SSI) solution for the Hiero ecosystem. The project delivers a complete set of applications and tools that enable issuance, management, and verification of verifiable credentials using global identity standards, while serving as a baseline reference implementation for Hiero / Hedera-based identity solutions.

The Heka Identity Platform is intended to speed up adoption of decentralized identity within the Hiero ecosystem and provide a practical, standards-aligned example for developers, integrators, and community members.

Join us for a meetup exploring Hiero ([https://github.com/hiero-ledger](https://github.com/hiero-ledger)), an open-source, vendor-neutral distributed ledger technology (DLT) stack that powers the Hedera Network. In this session, Hendrik Ebbers ([https://github.com/hendrikebbers](https://github.com/hendrikebbers)) will demonstrate how easy it is to deploy a Hiero-based network for either public or private use.

The live demo will show how to spin up a network and build a simple application that connects to it using one of the available SDKs. Attendees will learn how an application communicates with the network and submits transactions in real time.

This meetup is ideal for developers interested in learning how to deploy decentralized networks and build applications that interact with them using Hiero.

title: ANS, Agents & Consensus: HCS for verifiable AI Identity
description:
Join HOL, GoDaddy, and the Hiero community for a technical workshop on new draft specifications for verifiable AI agent identity. The session will introduce Universal Agent ID (UAID / HCS-14), the new ANS profile for DNS-based agent discovery, and HCS-27, a draft standard for publishing Merkle tree checkpoints from transparency logs to Hiero Consensus Service. Attendees will learn how ANS agents can remain rooted in DNS while becoming easier to resolve across ecosystems, and how registry history can be independently verified over time using public checkpoint commitments.

You can dial-in to this event [using this Zoom link](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09).

title: Lineth Overview & Use Cases: Inside the Production-Grade ZK Rollup Stack
description:
[With the announcement of Lineth joining Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust as an incubating project](https://www.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/blog/announcing-lineth-a-production-grade-zk-rollup-stack-joins-linux-foundation-decentralized-trust), we're opening the hood on the full stack in our first community Technical Deep Dive.

Lineth is a production-grade, EVM-equivalent zk-rollup stack for Ethereum - the same codebase that has powered Linea Mainnet since July 2023, finalizing over 300 million transactions and generating more than 416,000 zero-knowledge proofs with 99.98% sequencer uptime. It is now in a vendor-neutral, open source home under LFDT, governed by a Technical Steering Committee and has over 30 project maintainers.

This session is your entry point into the architecture, the community, and the roadmap.

Agenda:

* Welcome & Housekeeping
* Why Lineth
* Use cases & Interoperability
* High Level Architecture Overview
* Roadmap
* Open Discussions & Q&A

Stay tuned in #lineth-general on [LFDT Discord](https://discord.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/) for updates and to join the community.

title: Quantum Threat Landscape: Where We Stand and How to Prepare
description:
Quantum computing is no longer a distant threat. Improvements in hardware design, new algorithmic breakthroughs, and expert surveys now put a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer sooner than the industry is prepared for. Elliptic curve signatures and key exchange, RSA, and many ZK proof systems are vulnerable, where they underpin not just blockchains, but financial infrastructure, identity systems, enterprise software, and the internet itself.

However, the industry isn't standing still. In this workshop, Zain Cheng (CTO, Horizen Labs) and Tommaso Gagliardoni (Cryptography Research Manager, Horizen Labs) will give the LFDT community a comprehensive look at where the quantum migration stands today across blockchain ecosystems, traditional finance, government, and enterprise, and what you can do to prepare regardless of the stack you're building on.

The Threat Landscape: What quantum computers actually break, and what they don't. Shor's algorithm and elliptic curve cryptography. Grover's algorithm and symmetric/hash security. Why "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks make this urgent right now.

**Please note: This event is being shared with our entire global community. If you're interested in this content but can't attend the event live, feel free to sign up and we will send you a link to the recording after the meetup is over.**

title: 🧉 Mate Talk | Latency vs. AI: The new Trade-off in Live Streaming
description:
🧉 **Mate Talk is coming!**

**Latency vs. AI: The New Trade-Off in Live Streaming**
For the last five years, live streaming has been in a latency arms race — sub-three seconds, sub-one second, glass-to-glass parity with broadcast. We've spent real engineering capital getting there.

Now AI is showing up in the same pipeline: live translation, real-time dubbing, AI-generated sign language, multilingual captioning. Each one adds processing time, buffer requirements, and packaging complexity.

The two priorities are pulling against each other, and the industry hasn't fully admitted it.

In this Mate Talk we'll dig into what that trade-off actually looks like in production.

Join us with **David Hassoun, Olga Kornienko, Bhavesh Upadhyaya, Sean McCarthy, Andy Beach, and our special guest Neal Roberts.**

Mark your calendar and bring your energy.
**See you soon! 💚**

title: Lean Coffee: ¿Cómo toman decisiones las comunidades? Explorando la Sociocracia
description:
Las comunidades, equipos y organizaciones enfrentan un desafío común:

**¿Cómo tomar decisiones sin depender siempre de las mismas personas?**

A medida que los grupos crecen, aparecen preguntas complejas:

* ¿Quién debería decidir?
* ¿Cómo distribuimos responsabilidades?
* ¿Cómo fomentamos la participación sin volvernos burocráticos?
* ¿Cómo avanzamos sin quedar atrapados en reuniones interminables?

En este encuentro de AgileUY vamos a explorar una propuesta que busca abordar estos desafíos: **la Sociocracia**.

La Sociocracia es un modelo de gobernanza que propone nuevas formas de organizarse, distribuir autoridad y tomar decisiones de manera más participativa y efectiva.

⚠️ Importante: este no es un espacio para implementar cambios en AgileUY ni para tomar decisiones sobre la comunidad.

Nuestro objetivo es aprender juntos, conocer los principios fundamentales de la Sociocracia, entender cómo funciona y reflexionar sobre qué aprendizajes podría aportar a nuestras organizaciones, equipos y comunidades.

Si te interesan la agilidad, la facilitación, la autogestión, el liderazgo colaborativo o simplemente sentís curiosidad por nuevas formas de organización, este espacio es para vos.

title: Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026: anuncios y tendencias
description:
En esta edición, traemos lo más relevante de la Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026 junto con una sesión técnica enfocada en uno de los desafíos más comunes al adoptar IA generativa: cómo llevar agentes de IA a producción de forma escalable y gobernada.

📌 El equipo de Qubika participó en la Summit por tercer año consecutivo con stand, sesión técnica y presencia en la agenda oficial, y vuelve con aprendizajes frescos sobre qué está realmente maduro para producción y qué todavía requiere cautela.

🎤 **Charla 1 \| Recap Databricks Data \+ AI Summit 2026**
**Speaker: Aldis Stareczek \|** Solutions Architect & Databricks Champion @ Qubika
Vamos a traducir los anuncios del Summit a decisiones concretas: qué vale la pena explorar hoy, qué está listo para producción y cómo encaja en arquitecturas modernas.
El foco estará en novedades alrededor de AI Agents, Genie y Lakebase, con especial atención a modernización de plataformas de datos, migraciones a lakehouse y casos de uso de IA en entornos regulados y de tiempo real.

🎤 **Charla 2 \| De YAML a producción: Deploy de AI Agents con Databricks Asset Bundles**
Speaker invitado: Mauro Loprete \| Data Engineer @ F1RST \(Grupo Santander\) · Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional
Tu agente funciona en un notebook… ¿y ahora qué? Llevarlo a producción implica orquestar múltiples recursos: serving endpoints, vector search, jobs, permisos, monitoreo y despliegues por ambiente.
En esta charla veremos cómo Databricks Asset Bundles — recientemente renombrados como Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs) — permiten gestionar todo ese ciclo de vida de forma declarativa mediante YAML y CI/CD.
También recorreremos el ecosistema agéntico de Databricks en 2026, incluyendo Agent Bricks, Lakebase y Databricks Apps, a través de un caso real de un agente RAG con memoria desplegado de punta a punta.

👤 **Sobre el speaker invitado**
[Mauro Loprete](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mauro-loprete/) es estadístico de formación, trabaja con Databricks y dbt en producción en el sector financiero, y es docente de ciencia de datos y estadística computacional en la UdelaR.
Además, escribe sobre Data Engineering y Databricks en su blog, donde publica la serie “Databricks Tips” con aprendizajes prácticos del día a día con la plataforma.

title: Increasing Trust on Ethereum with ENS and Enscribe
description:
Most organizations on Ethereum are effectively anonymous. Contracts are deployed to nameless addresses, treasury wallets have no verifiable link to the org that controls them, and AI agents operate with no on-chain accountability. For protocols and DAOs trying to build credibility and operate transparently, this is a real problem — and it's one that existing tooling hasn't solved.

In this webinar, we'll walk through how organizations can easily create and manage on-chain identity for everything they deploy, using ENS as the identity layer supported by Enscribe ([https://www.enscribe.xyz/](https://www.enscribe.xyz/)). We'll show how protocols can name and manage their smart contracts, wallets, and agents under a unified namespace, making their on-chain presence verifiable, human-readable, and auditable.

title: Lineth Technical Deep Dive: Inside the Production-Grade ZK Rollup Stack
description:
With the announcement of Lineth ([https://github.com/LFDT-Lineth](https://github.com/LFDT-Lineth)) as a new Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust incubating project, we're opening the hood on the full stack in our first community Technical Deep Dive.

Lineth is a production-grade, EVM-equivalent zk-rollup stack for Ethereum - the same codebase that has powered Linea Mainnet since July 2023, finalizing over 300 million transactions and generating more than 416,000 zero-knowledge proofs with 99.98% sequencer uptime. It is now in a vendor-neutral, open source home under LFDT, governed by a Technical Steering Committee and with more than 30 project maintainers.

This session is your entry point into the architecture, the community, and the roadmap.

title: Architecture for Sustaining Open Source in Web 3
description:
Open source is the foundation of Web3, but most ecosystems still fund it like a series of short-term projects instead of long-term public infrastructure. As decentralized networks grow, the real challenge is no longer just building software. It is maintaining the critical code, tooling, standards, and contributor communities that keep the ecosystem secure, usable, and resilient.

This session explores what an architecture for sustaining open source in Web3 should look like. We will examine why traditional grant models often fall short, how maintenance differs from feature delivery, and why decentralized ecosystems need clearer coordination structures without recreating centralized control. The discussion will introduce models such as decentralized OSPOs and open maintenance frameworks as practical ways to align governance, funding, accountability, and contributor support.

Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how Web3 ecosystems can move from reactive funding toward intentional stewardship of open source infrastructure.

Learn more about this effort at: [https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/os-frontiers/tree/main](https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/os-frontiers/tree/main)

title: Tech Meetup | "AI in Production: What's Actually Shipping in Media Workflows"
description:
Everyone's talking about AI in the media workflow — QoE optimization, multi-CDN decisioning, auto-cropping, clip and highlight generation. The demos look great. But the real question is: what's actually running in production?
That's the focus of our next Tech Meetup (Thu, July 30): not the pitch decks, but the practice, where AI is genuinely deployed in live media operations and content workflows, what broke on the way there, and what still keeps a human in the loop.

**Three talks. Three real projects. No pitch decks.**

#### 🔴 "Faster Answers Under Pressure: An AI Root-Cause Co-Pilot for Streaming Ops"

**Nicolás Caballero @ Qualabs**
When quality drops, the dashboard turns red. Explaining why is the hard part — complex diagnostic work under pressure. We'll share how we put an LLM in that loop: how to trust it at 3am when it's confident and wrong, how to keep it cost-effective, and where AI actually earns its place versus where it's just overhead.

#### ✂️ "Pass, Fail, or Ask a Human: AI Quality Control for Video at Scale"

**Emil Santurio @ Qualabs**
Producing highlights at scale means every clip needs a quality check before it airs. Clean cuts. Right moment. On-brand.
But here's the thing: quality isn't one thing. Some checks are mechanical rules. Some need you to actually look at the frame. Some are genuinely subjective and editorial.
The real challenge isn't "use AI" — it's knowing which tool fits each check. Pick the wrong one and you either miss errors or burn cost and trust.
We'll share the honest lessons from putting this into production: which checks we let code handle, which needed computer vision, which still need a human, and what we'd do differently.

#### 🌍 "From Voice to Subtitle to Sign Language"

**Alexander Leschinsky @ G&L**
Accessibility at scale isn't a feature — it's a workflow. Alexander is sharing how sign language (BSL, ASL, and now German Sign Language) is being integrated into professional live and on-demand encoding, subtitling, and delivery. Working with UK-based Signapse, putting sign language on equal footing with subtitles. The honest part: what works, what's harder than expected, and how it changes your infrastructure.

Know someone who'd enjoy these conversations? **Share this post!**

title: Más allá del Hype: cómo construir mejores productos con IA
description:
**¿La IA llegó para romper el agilismo o para potenciarlo?**

La conversación sobre IA suele quedar atrapada entre el entusiasmo por las nuevas herramientas y la presión por incorporarlas cuanto antes.

Pero hay dos desafíos muy distintos que hoy enfrentan los equipos.

El primero es **cómo aprovechar la IA para potenciar el ciclo de desarrollo de producto**: estrategia, discovery, delivery, investigación, priorización y colaboración.

El segundo es **cuándo tiene sentido incorporar capacidades de IA dentro del producto para mejorar la propuesta de valor, y cuándo solo añade complejidad.**

Trabajar con IA exige experimentar, aprender rápido y tomar decisiones en un contexto de alta incertidumbre. Afortunadamente, esos son principios que la agilidad ha promovido desde siempre.

En esta meetup compartiremos aprendizajes y criterios prácticos para decidir qué vale la pena probar, qué adoptar y qué dejar pasar.

Porque el desafío ya no es usar IA por moda. Es utilizarla para construir mejores productos, tomar mejores decisiones y generar impacto.

Nos encontramos de forma **virtual por Google Meet.** Una vez que se anoten, les llega la invitación con el enlace.

title: 🧉 Mate Talk | "AI in Media: Your asset travels. Its context doesn't"
description:
🧉 Mate Talk is coming!

**AI in Media: Your Asset Travels. Its Context Doesn't.**
Every AI tool you plug into your media pipeline shows up knowing nothing about your library, and it stays that way. Your asset moves from tool to tool, handoff to handoff, but the context around it doesn't. It gets rebuilt from scratch every single time, so nothing ever compounds.

And there's a second layer to this that's less about the tools and more about us: we're generating 100-page docs with AI, then handing them straight back to AI to tell us what's in them, because nobody's actually going to read them. The knowledge exists somewhere. Our expertise doesn't grow.

So the real question: **how do you maintain and grow context and expertise in a world where the data and the tooling are temporary?**

Join us with **David Hassoun, Olga Kornienko, Bhavesh Upadhyaya, Sean McCarthy, Andy Beach, and JP Saibene**
for this one 👏🏼

We put this two weeks before IBC on purpose — this is the conversation we want to be having before we walk onto that floor.

See you on the 27th 🧉
Mark your calendar and bring your energy.
See you soon! 💚

title: 🎙️ Tech Meetup | C2PA on the road to IBC 2026!
description:
**C2PA on the Road to IBC 2026!**
Content authenticity is having a moment, AI-generated media, deepfakes, the growing question of "is this real?"
C2PA is the open standard trying to answer that: a cryptographically signed record of where a piece of media came from and whether it's been touched since.

That's the focus of our next Tech Meetup, ahead of IBC 2026: Qualabs and Unified Streaming sharing what we've actually been building on C2PA.

Our speakers:
**Pablo** **Flores** (VP of Engineering @ Qualabs) and **Valentijn Siebrands**
(@ Unified Streaming).

**Valentijn Talk \| "The Nutrition Label for Media: C2PA at the Packaging Stage"**
In the AI era, knowing where content comes from and whether it can be trusted matters more than ever.
C2PA acts like a modern “nutrition label” for media, carrying verifiable information about its origin and history. With Unified Streaming, those Content Credentials can be added dynamically at the packaging stage, for live and VOD — late enough to reflect the final stream, but early enough to preserve transparency before delivery.

Pablo Talk \| "**C2PA for Live Media, Upstream**
**Signing and validation in c2pa-rs, the Common Media Library, and dash.js"**
C2PA is an open, public spec, but the trip from reading it to running it across a real streaming pipeline is long - and for live, longer still. We made it and put the code where everyone can reach it: c2pa-rs, the SVTA Common Media Library, and dash.js. We'll show how to sign live video, how to validate it in the browser for live and VOD, and what's coming next.

📆 Thursday, September 3rd

title: Introducing the IPRAM Lab for Tokenized Regulated Asset Markets
description:
The tokenisation of regulated real-world assets has led to multiple institutional implementations of the same financial instruments, each operating on its own infrastructure with few shared patterns for how those infrastructures interoperate. As a result, tokenised assets remain confined to the environment they were issued in, accessible only to counterparties already inside the same institutional perimeter.

The IPRAM Lab ([https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM](https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM)) develops open implementation patterns for the interoperation of tokenised real-world regulated financial assets and the markets they participate in. This session introduces the lab's mission, scope, and the initial interoperability challenges it aims to address. All interested parties are invited to join!

title: VeltoraCore - The Optimization Layer for Fragmented Markets
description:
Join us for a discussion about the new VeltoraCore lab that is building a pair-coin, system-agnostic optimization engine that jointly coordinates user execution and LP participation in a single feasibility framework. A lightweight Proof-of-Optimization (PoO) mechanism cryptographically commits optimized batch outcomes to external system states, enabling verifiable cross-system settlement. Simulations on the ETH–USD pair show superior retained execution and materially lower user fees relative to benchmarks, while delivering liquidity-provider returns higher with reduced volatility.

This is a great opportunity to talk to the developers about what they're building and to learn how to get involved if this sounds interesting.

More about the VeltoraCore lab is at: [https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/veltoracore](https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/veltoracore)

title: Migraciones de código legacy: potenciado el testing con IA
description:
Hoy en día, gracias al uso de asistentes de IA, se hizo más viable migrar sistemas legacy, como aplicaciones basadas en COBOL o RPG, a tecnologías modernas. Esto sucede gracias a que estos asistentes reducen costos del desarrollo al ayudar a entender el código legacy y regenerarlo en la nueva arquitectura. Sin embargo, el testing sigue siendo uno de los mayores obstáculos, especialmente porque en estos contextos la documentación es escasa o está desactualizada, y las personas con el conocimiento están poco disponibles o ya no están en la empresa, lo que dificulta verificar el comportamiento esperado.

En esta charla v**eremos una metodología que diseñamos en Abstracta para abordar este desafío con el apoyo de IA,** y veremos los aprendizajes que obtuvimos en los primeros proyectos realizando este tipo de migraciones. Esta metodología aborda el desafío como un problema de “characterization testing”, pudiendo generar cobertura en el sistema original a nivel de pruebas automatizadas y a nivel de pruebas funcionales a nivel de usuario. Esta cobertura se genera a partir del código y la documentación disponible, y se valida con las personas con conocimiento de negocio y desarrollo. Lo importante es poder generar outputs en ambas versiones del sistema que se puedan comparar, para encontrar diferencias en el comportamiento. A este enfoque se lo complementa con una comprensión dinámica a través de observabilidad. Presentamos cómo implementamos estos enfoques sobre Tero, nuestra plataforma open-source que desarrollamos para dar soporte a agentes de IA que asisten a los testers, y demostramos su uso con ejemplos concretos de un sistema COBOL.

Si bien todavía estamos recolectando métricas, los primeros resultados indican proyectos de migración más viables y beneficios tangibles al aplicar IA al testing. **Esta sesión propone repensar la IA como una aliada del tester, no solo del desarrollador.**

title: Open Source Climate Accounting: What Exists, What's Missing+Where To Contribute
description:
Climate accounting increasingly depends on systems that were never designed to work together. Registries use different standards and data models. The same activity can appear across multiple systems. Measurement data may come from sensors, satellite observations, models, or manual reporting, often with limited provenance or no straightforward way for downstream users to verify how a claim was produced.

These are not only reporting problems but they are problems of interoperability, provenance, reconciliation and trust between independent systems.

A substantial amount of open-source work already exists to address them, but much of it remains fragmented or little known outside the communities that built it. This session will map that landscape: what is already available, what is mature enough to use today, what remains experimental and where meaningful technical contributions are still needed.

The aim is not to argue that blockchain is the answer to climate accounting. It is to look practically at where distributed ledgers, verifiable data, open standards and other open-source infrastructure can solve specific problems or where they cannot.

Structure - The session would begin with a short framing of the technical problems behind climate and impact accounting: provenance, reconciliation, double counting, interoperability and verification across organisational boundaries.

From there, members of the LF Decentralized Trust community could walk through existing open-source projects and frameworks, explaining what they were built to solve, how mature they are and where they are being used today.

The final part would focus on the gaps: problems that remain unsolved, areas where maintainers would welcome contributions and practical ways for developers, researchers and organisations to get involved.

The IEEE ClimateChain Global Hackathon ([https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/](https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/)) would be introduced as one of those routes to contribution.

The goal is for participants to leave with a clearer picture of what already exists, which problems are genuinely open and where their time and technical skills could have the greatest value.

title: Policy-Checked, Attributable, Revocable, Provable AI Agent Authorization
description:
AI agents are entering production with long-lived API keys in their environment, broader access than any task needs, and no answer to the questions: Which agent performed this action? Under whose authority?

A single prompt injection, leaked credential, or runaway agent can quickly become a security incident. Security reviews delay deployments, and auditors are often left without sufficient evidence to understand what happened.

Existing security infrastructure was not designed for autonomous AI agents. Identity providers register agents but do not authorize every action, secret managers distribute credentials to workloads, and API gateways route requests without making authorization decisions.

This talk introduces Caracal, an open source AI authorization system currently being developed through the LFDT LFX Mentorship program and supported by GitHub, Microsoft, and Vercel. We'll discuss what authority means for AI agents, why authorization must move beyond credentials, and how we designed Caracal's architecture to provide policy-based authorization, attribution, revocation, and auditability for agent actions.

The session will cover:

* Why traditional API key and identity models are insufficient for AI agents
* What authority means in autonomous AI systems
* The architectural design behind Caracal
* Practical approaches to securing AI agents in production

The meetup will be presented by the Caracal team, Ryan Madhuwala and Shubham Sharma.

Our LFX mentees, Mohammad Ali Haider and Ashutosh Singh, will also present their work on the project. If you're interested in AI security and secure agent infrastructure, we'd be happy to have you join us.

title: AI × Decentralized Trust: Kickoff of the LFDT AI Working Group
description:
AI is already in our pull requests — and agentic AI needs exactly what we build. Let's talk about both.

AI has already arrived in our repositories. It writes patches, reviews pull requests, and is often the first thing a newcomer asks about a codebase they don't understand yet. At the same time, agentic AI is arriving from the other direction — as a use case. Autonomous agents need identities they can prove, credentials others can verify, and a way to pay each other for the things they consume. That is our home turf.

LFDT has no shared position on either side of this yet. This meeting launches the LFDT AI Working Group and sets its scope together with the people who will do the work.

We will open three questions:

**How do we use AI when building LFDT projects? What** is allowed, what has to be disclosed, and what does it mean for provenance, licensing, DCO sign-off, and security review? The Linux Foundation's existing generative AI guidance is the floor — the question is what our projects need on top of it.

**Can AI help us grow our communities?** Review bots like CodeRabbit, automated triage of good first issues, and onboarding assistants promise a shorter path from first-time contributor to committer. Do they actually deliver that, or do they just add noise for maintainers to clean up? And if we want them, who runs them and who pays?

**Where does our work connect to the AI world?** Two neighbours at the Linux Foundation matter most: the Agentic AI Foundation (MCP, goose, AGENTS.md) and the x402 Foundation, which stewards payments over HTTP for agents. Agentic identity and agent-to-agent commerce are exactly where DLT belongs — and where LFDT projects should be visible.

This is a kickoff, not a keynote. Bring your opinions, your objections, and the problems you already have. We want to leave with an initial scope, a meeting cadence, and named volunteers for the first work streams.

Open to everyone: maintainers, contributors, TSC members, LFDT staff, and anyone from the wider Linux Foundation AI ecosystem. No prior involvement in LFDT required.

title: Del Lakehouse a la AI: Lakebase + coding agents en Databricks
description:
Databricks está evolucionando mucho más allá del mundo de los datos.
En este nuevo encuentro del Databricks User Group Montevideo vamos a explorar cómo la plataforma permite pasar de almacenar, transformar y gobernar datos a construir aplicaciones directamente sobre ellos, y cómo la IA está cambiando la forma misma de desarrollar en Databricks.

🎤 **Charla 1 \| Explorando Lakebase viniendo del desarrollo de software**
**Speaker: Virginia Rodríguez \|** Qubika

Un recorrido por Lakebase, la base de datos PostgreSQL integrada al ecosistema Databricks: qué propone, cuándo tiene sentido usarla y qué habilitan features como branching y synced tables, con foco en servir datos del Lakehouse para consulta interactiva desde aplicaciones. Todo desde la mirada de quien llega con un background de desarrollo de software.

🎤 **Charla 2 \| Desarrollar con IA en Databricks: Coding agents\, Agent Skills y Genie**
**Speaker invitado: Francisco Esteves Muñoz \|** F1RST (Grupo Santander)

Databricks está incorporando nuevas capacidades de IA que están cambiando la forma de desarrollar e interactuar con la plataforma. Veremos cómo combinar coding agents, Agent Skills y Databricks CLI con herramientas como Genie Code, y cómo capacidades como Genie Spaces amplían este enfoque hacia el acceso y análisis de datos. Un approach práctico: cómo preparar los repositorios y qué aprendizajes deja este nuevo modelo de trabajo.

La idea del meetup es ver cómo estas piezas se combinan para crear una plataforma cada vez más end to end, acercando mundos que tradicionalmente trabajaban por separado: datos, desarrollo de software, AI y producto.
Habrá demos, ejemplos reales, arquitectura y espacio para intercambiar experiencias con la comunidad.

🔹 **¿A quién está dirigido?**
Si trabajás en Data, Engineering, Software Development, AI o simplemente querés entender hacia dónde está evolucionando Databricks, este meetup es para vos.

🍕🍻 Además, nuestro equipo de cocina nos recibe como siempre con un tapeo que ya es un clásico de la casa.

**Sobre Databricks**
Databricks es una plataforma unificada y basada en la nube para ingeniería de datos, analítica, machine learning e IA, construida sobre Apache Spark. Ayuda a las organizaciones a optimizar el procesamiento de datos a gran escala, acelerar el desarrollo de modelos de IA y facilitar la colaboración entre equipos de datos.
[www.databricks.com](https://www.databricks.com)

**Sobre Qubika**
Qubika ayuda a las empresas a evolucionar de Digital Native a AI Native. Somos Databricks Gold Partner con más de 250 ingenieros certificados y más de 1.000 expertos en Estados Unidos y Latinoamérica. En 2026 fuimos elegidos Databricks Latin America Innovation Partner of the Year, y reconocidos por Constellation Research entre las 8 principales consultoras de AI del mundo y por el Financial Times entre las empresas de mayor crecimiento de América.
[www.qubika.com](https://www.qubika.com)

title: FabricOps: Operating Hyperledger Fabric Networks on Kubernetes
description:
[FabricOps is an LF Decentralized Trust Lab](https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/FabricOps) that provides a Kubernetes operator and CLI for provisioning and operating multi-organization Hyperledger Fabric networks from declarative, Fablo-style configuration.

In this meetup, Pereowei Daniel will introduce the motivation behind FabricOps, especially the gap between local Fabric development with tools like Fablo and production-oriented Kubernetes deployment. The session will cover how FabricOps reconciles Fabric network intent into Kubernetes resources, including Fabric CA enrollment, MSP/TLS material, orderers, peers, channels, Chaincode-as-a-Service lifecycle, observability, and federated organization joining.

The meetup will also discuss how FabricOps can complement existing ecosystem efforts such as Fablo, Fabric Operator, hlf-operator, and Hyperledger Bevel, and where the project may fit into the broader Fabric and Fabric-X roadmap.

description:

title: OWASP Meetup - Octubre
description:
**¡OWASP UY te invita a su próximo Meetup!**

**Andrés Pastorini**: *Seguridad en APIs: Al infinito y más allá de Bearer Tokens. MFA Step-Up, PKCE y protección de clientes móviles*
En un ecosistema donde las APIs sostienen el core del negocio, un header "Authorization: Bearer \ " estándar puede no alcanzar. Esta charla aborda patrones avanzados de seguridad aplicados al diseño e integración de APIs críticas:
-Solicitar re-autenticación o segundo factor dinámicamente según la criticidad de la transacción.
-Seguridad en APIs Mobile & PKC, mitigando riesgos en clientes públicos, almacenamiento seguro de tokens y mitigación de llamadas maliciosas desde apps modificadas. Ofuscación, App Attestation y DPoP.

**Alejandro Martínez:** *Tecnología vs Humanos*
En esta charla analizaremos cómo la brecha entre la sofisticación técnica y la realidad operativa diaria convierte al factor humano en el eslabón clave —ya sea como el vector de entrada más vulnerable o como la primera línea de defensa efectiva—. Revisaremos el impacto real de estos incidentes en el ecosistema empresarial y por qué la verdadera resiliencia no se compra en una licencia de software, sino que se construye en la cultura organizacional.

**¿Cuándo?** Lunes 26/10, 18:30.

title: Measuring Ledgers With The Blockchain Decentralisation Index Lab
description:
The new Blockchain Decentralisation Index Lab is an open source tool kit for measuring the decentralisation of distributed ledgers, layer by layer — consensus, tokenomics, network, software, and beyond.

The lab develops and maintains a suite of open source tools that collect data from live blockchain systems, parse it into a common format, and compute decentralisation metrics over it. Each tool targets a distinct layer of the stack and shares a common pipeline architecture (collect → parse → map to entities → apply metrics → publish).

Learn more about the Lab, how to use it and how to get involved in this online event. You can also find out more about the Lab at: [https://github.com/Blockchain-Decentralisation-Index](https://github.com/Blockchain-Decentralisation-Index)

You are also welcome to join the #bdi channel on the LFDT Discord at: [https://discord.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/](https://discord.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/)

title: Building Privacy Preserving Token Applications Using Panurus
description:
Panurus ([https://github.com/LFDT-Panurus](https://github.com/LFDT-Panurus)) is an open-source framework for building token-based applications that preserve transactional privacy while remaining fully auditable and interoperable across ledgers. In this talk, we'll walk through how Panurus's driver-based architecture lets developers plug in different token technologies — from Fabtoken to zero-knowledge schemes — behind a common transaction lifecycle (Request → Assemble → Sign → Commit), and how this enables privacy-preserving applications without locking you into a single blockchain or cryptographic scheme.

We'll also spotlight two mentorship programs currently pushing Panurus's capabilities forward:

**\- EVM Network Driver** — extending Panurus with support for EVM-compatible chains, bringing privacy-preserving tokens to Ethereum and its ecosystem.
**\- zkat\-snark Driver** — introducing a zk-SNARK-based anonymous token driver, expanding Panurus's toolkit for confidential, provably-correct transactions.

Come see how these efforts are shaping Panurus's roadmap, and how you can get involved.

**Zoom Meeting Link**: [https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09)

title: Webinar with Cosmos Labs: Designing Tokenized Deposits for a Multi-Ledger Future
description:
Join us for a webinar with Cosmos Labs, an LFDT general member, on Designing Tokenized Deposits for a Multi-Ledger Future. Most tokenized deposit initiatives start within a single institution or consortium, but the architecture choices banks make today will determine how effectively deposits can reach new markets and power new use cases. This session examines how an interoperability protocol fits into a tokenized deposit stack, covering how deposits and data can be exchanged across ledgers without intermediaries, key use cases like cross-border payments, programmable escrow, and collateral mobility, and what changes when interoperability is built in from the start. Designed for CTOs, digital asset leads, and engineering teams planning or running tokenized deposit programs.

The webinar will take place on Wednesday, **November 13** at **7AM PST/10AM EST/16:00 CET/8:30 PM IST**

Please register here: https://zoom.us/webinar/register/8716754539090/WN_vOKR45ECSl2Pp0NpMSAskw

title: An Architectural Deep Dive into New CLPR (Cross-Ledger Protocol) Lab
description:
**LFDT Labs Introduces CLPR - An Architectural Deep Dive into CLPR (Cross-Ledger Protocol)**

Join us for an in-depth technical session introducing CLPR (Cross-Ledger Protocol), a newly approved open-source project hosted under the LF Decentralized Trust Labs.
Traditional cross-chain bridges often introduce security vulnerabilities, liquidity locking, and third-party trust assumptions. CLPR takes a fundamental shift: enabling direct, asynchronous ledger-to-ledger communication using cryptographic state proofs.

In this Meetup, we will explore:
**Architectural Overview (20–30 min)**
The problem with traditional bridges.
Core trust model.
Breakdown of the protocol layers.
How to adapt CLPR for arbitrary EVM, non-EVM, public, and enterprise ledger types.

**Implementation Deep Dive (45–60 min)**
Hiero Native Implementation
Besu Reference Implementation

**Live Software Demo and Q&A (30 min)**
Live Demonstration: Watching CLPR execute cross-ledger state proof verification in real time.

**Q&A and Community Discussion and get involved in the LFDT Lab.**

**Zoom Meeting Link**: [https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09)
